Casilida DeAniasie.wikitext:
{{ImperiumPortal}}
'''Casilida DeAniasie''' was a [[Rogue Trader]], who took part in the [[Great Crusade]] and discovered the [[Forge World]] [[Xana|Xana II]].{{Fn|1}}

==History==
This occurred in 843.[[M30]], after her ship was flung far off-course after fighting [[Fra'al|Fra'al Corsairs]]. The [[Rogue Trader]], however, later intercepted a trio of automata warships, at the edge of the inter-galactic void. After making contact, the warships greeted Aniasie and offered her aid. When she accepted, the Rogue Trader was guided to the [[Forge World]] [[Xana|Xana II]], where her ship began to be repaired. Once the Forge World had finished, Aniasie departed with an offer of diplomatic exchange between the [[Imperium]] and the '''Sovereign Forge Domain of Xana'''. This later led Xana II and its domain to fully join the Imperium.{{Fn|1}}

Cassia Orsellio.wikitext:
{{ImperiumPortal}}
{{QuoteBox
|quote = '''''"Fear not, I have my Navigator skills to call upon. Statistically speaking, you are far more likely to perish in battle. Oh, I mean, that came out wrong..."'''''{{Fn|2}}}}
'''Cassia Orsellio''' is a young [[Navigator]], who has made the [[Koronus Expanse]] her home.{{Fn|1}}
==History==
She was originally raised in secret on a restricted-access station by [[House Orsellio|her Navigator House]] and Orsellio does not know who her real parents are. During that time, all the young Navigator knew was endless years of study and the duty toward her House, that weighed down on Orsellio's fragile shoulders. As a result of living in a gilded cage, she knew nothing outside of its walls - until a twist of fate snatched Orsellio away from it. Now freed much sooner than her mentors had planned, Orsellio was left alone to face the cruelty of the [[Galaxy]]. The Navigator's innate powers would dismay those around her and drove away Orsellio's friends and foes alike. What her current future holds is unclear. Will Orsellio break free from the bondage of hopes and ideas that are not her own, or is she perhaps destined to become an obedient cog in the soulless machine that is the [[Imperium]]? Only the stars can see the future...{{Fn|1}}

==Navigator Abilities==
Cassia navigates the warp like all Navigators using her Third Eye. However, to her, this appears as a confusing kaleidoscope of colour. To focus on the specific path to take, she paints what she sees onto a canvas, the path becoming more clear as she does so.{{Fn|3a}} For the colour red, she uses the blood of her servants.{{Fn|3b}}

'''Cassian Vaughn'''{{Fn|1a}} was a [[Salamanders]] [[Legion Master|Lord Commander]] during the [[Unification Wars]], [[Great Crusade]], and [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|1}} He eventually became the leader of the "[[Disciples of the Flames]]".{{Fn|2}}

===Overview===
Cassian was the first Lord Commander of the XVIIIth Legion (later to be known as the Salamanders) before the coming of their [[Primarch]] [[Vulkan]], during his time as Lord Commander he would come become friends with Primarch [[Horus]] of the [[Luna Wolves]]. {{Fn|3a}} Mortally wounded in battle against [[Orks]] in the [[Taras Division]], he'd be held in high esteem by the rest of the Legion, after his wounding Vulkan fashioned for him a unique suit of [[Dreadnought]] armour known as the '''Dracos Revenant'''. This unique sarcophagus of unparalleled resilience that was forged in nigh-impregnable alloy that was said to be a relic of the [[Dark Age of Technology]].{{Fn|1b}}{{Fn|1c}}

As the years went on, Cassian (now '''Cassian Dracos''') began to suffer from the mental dilution common in those entombed as a Dreadnought. He began to only be awoken in the most dire of circumstances. Such a case arose during the [[Drop Site Massacre]], where he spearheaded an attack against the enemy and later slaughtered vast amounts of Traitors during the encirclement of loyalist forces. Eventually, Horus would emerge into the battle and join his warriors in slaughtering the loyalist, Cassian would see Horus before Horus saw him and so would lead a charge with fellow Salamanders against Horus, slaying members of the [[Justaerin]] before Horus would see him. When Horus did see Cassian there was a resemblance of recognition in his eyes before slamming [[Worldbreaker]] into Cassian, sending his world dark. {{Fn|3b}}

Badly damaged, Dracos' sarcophagus was buried beneath Isstvan V. It was later recovered by the crew of the [[Ebon Drake]], and upon reawakening Dracos informed his brethren that Vulkan lived. Dracos later commanded his mixed force of Salamanders, [[Raven Guard]], [[Iron Hands]], and [[Iron Warriors]] -known as the "[[Disciples of the Flames]]"- to a significant victory in the [[Mezoan Campaign]].{{Fn|2}}

'''Cassilus''' was a [[Rogue Trader]], who was active in the [[Koronus Expanse]].{{Fn|1}}
==History==
In 500.[[M41]] she attempted to dock on [[Footfall]], which was ruled by the tyrannic [[Recidivist]], [[Tarn Marvolus]]. While the [[Koronus Expanse|Expanse]]'s [[Rogue Traders]] had been content to allow Marvolus to control Footfall, this allowed him to grow too bold and arrogant. He finally overstepped, however, after he demanded that Cassilus pay him personal tribute for docking on his world. The Rogue Trader replied that she would "pay a tribute of the kind she only paid to the greatest kings of untamed worlds". Afterwards, the four quarters of Marvolous's body were later found in the four farthest points of Footfall.{{Fn|1}}

Castinus.wikitext:
{{OrdoHereticusPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was an [[Inquisitor]] of the newly created [[Ordo Hereticus]] when he led a quarantine team to search a missing [[League of Blackships|Black Ship]] that was discovered in the [[Medrenax Nebula]].  Within it he found a bloodbath, as the Black Ship was filled with the mangled bodies of its crew and passengers, save for the powerful [[psyker]]s known as the [[Apex Twins]].  When Castinus asked if they were responsible for the massacre aboard the Black Ship, the physically weakened Apex Twins readily admitted to doing so, without any hesitation.  For reasons known only to himself, Castinus did not kill the Twins, perhaps because he was unknowingly influenced by their physic power, and instead brought them to the [[Inquisition]] fortress of [[Nemesis Tessera]] for analysis and study.  This would have horrifying consequences, though, as the Apex Twins were able to regain their full power and freed themselves from their cells.  What followed was a massacre, as the Twins began a murderous rampage that saw almost a thousand Inquisitorial troopers slaughtered as well as scores of full Inquisitors, before they made their escape.  It is not known if Castinus was among those who were killed.{{Fn|1}}

Castus (Daemonblood).wikitext:
'''Castus''' was a [[Space Marine Sergeant]] of the [[Ultramarines]] [[Chapter]] [[2nd Company (Ultramarines)|Second Company]]. Isolated by the [[daemon]] [[Parmenides]] during the battle to reclaim the [[heretic]] city of [[Saafir]] along with [[Battle Sister]] [[Aescarion]], Castus was scoured of his memories and faith, which opened the door for his fall to [[Nurgle]]. Aescarion spent years searching for and fighting Castus to try and bring him to repent. Her mission was a success, as Castus chose to come back to his master on  Saafir and detonate an [[Exterminatus|Exterminatus warhead]] concealed inside his decaying body, destroying Parmenides and putting an end to his control on over a dozen worlds.{{Fn|1}}

Caudeus.wikitext:
{{UltramarinesPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was a [[Space Marine Sergeant|Sergeant]] in the [[Ultramarines]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]] who took part in the [[Battle of Calth]] and later the '''Underground War''' beneath its surface. 

It was during that war underground that the squadrons of Caudeus and Sergeant [[Tynon]] became separated from their Legion while fighting in '''Vault-Vexillium''', when the [[Word Bearers]] began to break through the Ultramarines' battle lines. They soon found themselves surrounded by the advancing Word Bearers, and their situation was even more critical because Caudeus's squadron held the relic [[Space Marine Standard|Honour Standard]], known as [[Guilliman's First Oath]]. Realizing that the Word Bearers would seize the Honour Standard after they were killed, the two Sergeants agreed to go on the attack and attempt a breakout that would allow one of their number to escape with the relic. They went on to sell their lives dearly against the Word Bearers, which allowed [[Olmenus]], one of Caudeus's squadron, to escape down a service chute with the Honour Standard.{{Fn|1}}

Caul (Redemption Cult).wikitext:
{{NecromundaPortal}}
'''Caul the Fallen''' was a [[Necromunda (planet)|Necromunda]] [[Cult of Redemption|Redemptionist]], who brought the Cult variation known as the [[Red Redemption]] to the [[Hive World]]{{Fn|1b}} in 893.[[M40]].{{Fn|1a}} 
==History==
According to legends, he was born on some far flung [[Hive World]] and, upon learning of the [[Redemption Cult]], Caul took to the stars to spread its faith. He eventually reached [[Necromunda (planet)|Necromunda]]'s wastelands and began spreading his variation of the Cult, which became known as the [[Red Redemption]]. Wherever Caul went, Red Redemption Cults were created and his righteous soldiers helped him win countless battles against [[Heretic]]s, monsters and [[Mutant]]s alike. These include destroying the [[Ember Lords]] of the [[Yearning Deeps]] and the [[Dark Arbitrators]], who once ruled the lost [[Hive]]s of [[Spoilshadow]]. In the centuries since his death, the Red Redemption has taken root within Necromunda's Hives and even now, Caul's legend is still remembered. His masked visage stares down from tumbled spires and broken wrecks on the Hive World, which are a constant reminder that the glory of the Redemption lives eternal.{{Fn|1b}}

{{UltramarinesPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was a [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] in the [[Ultramarines]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]] during the [[Horus Heresy]]; he was later given the title [[Force Commander|Lieutenant-Commander]] when he led a battlegroup against the [[Warmaster]]'s forces. However, during their campaign, the battlegroup was imprisoned by the [[Necron Lord]] [[Trazyn the Infinite]], who used a [[Tesseract Labyrinth]] to place them in stasis vaults beneath his fortress on Solemnace. They were kept in Trazyn's collection of beings who had garnered the Necron Lord's interest until the [[Thirteenth Black Crusade]] began. When [[Abaddon the Despoiler]] personally led the [[Chaos]] forces invading [[Cadia]] to battle, Trazyn, who had come to the beleaguered world's defense, sought to aid the Imperium's shattered forces. After throwing a Tessereact Labyrinth near the Despoiler, the Necron Lord unleashed an army composed of the Imperium warriors he had captured, Cerantes's battlegroup among them{{Fn|1a}}. Only a second had passed for Cerantes, since his capture and though he realized something was amiss, he immediately led his battlegroup against the Despoiler's forces, as they wore the symbols of Chaos. The Lieutenant-Commander soon clashed with Abaddon himself, but was no match for the master of the [[Black Legion]], who easily killed Cerantes. Though they fought on after his death, Cerantes's battlegroup soon fell to the [[Black Legion]] as well.{{Fn|1b}}

'''The Changeling''' is an infamous [[Horror of Tzeentch]].

===Overview===
The Changeling has the ability to assume the shape of any creature to use for trickery, to sow mistrust and confusion, and while not in battle to play practical jokes on the unwary.{{Fn|1}} The Changeling has altered so many times that even he has forgotten his original appearance. Only the God [[Tzeentch]] remembers it, and keeps it secret as a means of controlling the Changeling. The Changeling's schemes are not limited to the mortal realm, and he has been known to play tricks on even [[Gods of Chaos]] themselves, such as cutting [[Slaanesh]]'s hair as the Dark Prince slept or putting [[Nurgling]]s on [[Khorne]]'s throne, creating a mess the next time the Blood God sat down.{{Fn|3}}

Roaming the [[galaxy]] and [[Warp]] alike in search of committing both practical jokes and devastating mayhem, the Changeling has appeared on the battlefield as a mirror-image of a hero, his comrades unable to tell the difference between the two until it was too late. It was the Changeling who in the image of [[Lord Solar Macharius]] ordered the retreat on [[Goranna]] just as the real [[Warmaster]] was about to direct his forces to the front line. As a [[Grot]], the Changeling sabotoged [[Warboss]] [[Gitsmasha]]'s favorite [[Shoota]], blowing the Warlord and his retinue to smithereens as soon as it was fired. On one occasion, the Changeling even took the shape of a [[Keeper of Secrets]] and answered the summoning of a traitorous [[Imperial Governor]] whose palace was besieged by [[Dark Angels]]. There, the Changeling traded the souls of the desperate man's daughters for a "powerful artifact" to turn the tide of the siege, but turned out to be a stolen [[Ravenwing]] teleporation beacon.{{Fn|3}}

The Changeling was dispatched by Tzeentch to extend the "gift" of annihilation to [[Ahriman]] once the [[Thousand Sons]] arch-sorcerer completed his [[Rubric of Ahriman#Second Rubric|Second Rubric]].{{Fn|4a}} In order to approach Ahriman, the Changeling killed and took the identity of a number of victims, but its disguise did not fool [[Ignis]]'s automaton Credence, which attacked the daemon but was quickly defeated.{{Fn|4b}} When the Changeling reached its intended target, however, Tzeentch stopped its minion, revealing that new schemes had been planned for Ahriman. The trickster contented itself by briefly revealing its true face to the sorcerer before erasing all memory of the encounter.{{Fn|4c}}

The Changeling proved instrumental in orchestrating the [[Siege of the Fenris System]] in the late [[41st Millennium]]. Disguising itself first as a [[Dark Angels]] [[Scout]] and later [[Sammael]], the Changeling convinced [[Azrael]] that the [[Space Wolves]] had become mutated and were responsible for attacks on Dark Angels targets across the Galaxy.{{Fn|5}}

The Changeling wields the [[Trickster's Staff]], which can mimic the weapons of his enemies.{{Fn|6}}

Chanthar.wikitext:
{{KhornePortal}}
'''Chanthar''' was a [[demagogue]] of the [[Chaos]] army who held the [[Voltis Citadel]] on [[Voltemand]] during the [[Sabbat Worlds Crusade]].{{Fn|1}}

==Biography==
Chanthar led a cult that worshiped [[Khorne]]. They would wear white robes but dipped in vats of blood. The majority of the men were offworlders, professional soldiers in service to the Archenemy. The cult had [[boltgun]]s and [[lasgun]]s, as well as [[Flak Armour|body armour]]. They also adorned themselves with sigils and runes of [[Khorne]] that were cut into their flesh.

Once Sergeant [[Cluggan]] of the [[Tanith First and Only]] breached the city walls, Chanthar turned a [[melta gun]] on himself, knowing that he had lost.{{Fn|1}}

Charities of Delphi.wikitext:
{{AdeptusMechanicusPortal}}
The '''Charities of Delphi''' are a triumvirate of [[Fabricator General]]s, who rule the [[Eastern Fringe]] [[Forge World]] [[Delphi (Forge World)|Delphi]].  

Lady Agaeleatrix, Charity of Splendour, currently resides on the Celestial Walkway - what remains of Delphi's artificial ring that once circled the planet. Lady Euryale, Magos Domina of the 5th moon, is the Fabricator-Locum of the Delphic Haven,  the highest of the Underlords of Delphi, formally under the banner of Lady Agaeleatrix {{Fn|1}} 

==History==
Composed of the [[Fabricator General]]s '''Euphrosinn''', '''Thilya''', and '''Agaeleatrix''', the Charities have had frequent beneficial dealings with the [[Rogue Trader]] [[Vileth Rey Aggranoza]]. This is due to Aggranoza believing that [[Delphi (Forge World)|Delphi]], is one of the few safe places in the [[Eastern Fringe|Fringe]] that will not question too deeply as to how he acquired his items. As a result, the Rogue Trader goes to the Forge World, whenever he has found something strange he wishes to sell. Though they have never met directly, the Charities have now developed such goodwill towards Aggranoza, that they will freely repair and refuel his ships whenever he visits.{{Fn|1}}

Charon.wikitext:
{{DarkAngelsPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[Lexicanium]] in the [[Dark Angels]] [[Chapter]] who served with the [[3rd Company (Dark Angels)|Third Company]] under [[Space Marine Captain|Master]] [[Belial]] during the [[Battle of Piscina IV]].{{Fn|1a}}

However, the Lexicanium was attached to the Third Company as [[Grand Master]] [[Azrael]]'s representative and Belial had no doubt, that Charon would report to the Grandmaster on how he conducted his campaign against the [[Orks]]. This weighed heavily on the Master's mind during the Battle{{Fn|1a}}, as after underestimating the invading Orks, he was forced to ask Charon to send a message to Azrael, asking for desperately needed reinforcements{{Fn|1b}}. Belial felt that the message, along with Charon's report of his actions against the Orks, would cause Azrael to make him relinquish his rank of Master and this caused him to later confront the Lexicanium. Charon assured Belial however, that Azrael had full faith in the Master's abilities and had only attached him to the Third Company, because the Grand Master believed Belial was destined for greater things within their Chapter. The Lexicaium then stated, that despite their setbacks with the Orks, Belial had given him no cause to question Azrael's belief in the Third Company Master.{{Fn|1a}}

Cherubael.wikitext:
[[File:Mtg-cherubael.jpg|thumb|300px|right|Cherubael, retinue of [[Inquisitor]] [[Eisenhorn]]{{Fn|7}}]]

'''Cherubael''' is a [[Daemon Prince]]. He was bound into a [[Daemonhost]] by [[Inquisitor]] [[Quixos]] and forced to join his retinue. Following Quixos's execution, he was rebound and pressed into service by Insquistor [[Eisenhorn]].{{Fn|4}}

==History==
While Cherubael has no known patron god, his exploits are known throughout the [[Imperium]]. In the [[Library Sanctus]] on [[Holy Terra]], the archive "[[Liber Malum]]" chronicles the history of this daemon. Cherubael's exploits include {{Fn|4}}:

* Enslaving the [[Fenestra]] star system for millennia, earning him the title "Death of Worlds".
* Enslaving the [[Kitarax Nebula]], whose people knew him as "The Scourge"{{Fn|4}}.
* Plunging the [[Gethme]] sector into unending war for 1000 years{{Fn|4}}.
* Committing mass genocide and driving the [[Ronja]] to extinction in a single night{{Fn|4}}.
* Leading the entire population of [[Medredax]] into ritual suicide{{Fn|4}}.
* Enslaving the feral world [[Clanar II]] for generations, whose populace performed millions of blood sacrifices to appease their "god"{{Fn|4}}.

When [[Inquisitor]] [[Quixos]] freed the Clanars from Cherubael's domination, he managed to bind the creature into the body of one of his warriors. At this point in his career, he was already well on his path of [[radicalism]], as the daemon sword [[Kharnagar]] had been pivotal to Cherubael's defeat.{{Fn|6}}

Years later, one of Cherubael's cults sprung up on [[Cadia]].  Calling itself the "Sons of Bael," the cult was a front for the study of the [[Pylon]]s on the planet. Using stolen security codes from the local Cadian Inquisitor [[Neve]], the cultists had been continuing their covert studies for many years. They had arisen some years before 338.M41, when Quixos had begun investigating the properties of [[Blackstone]], in the hope he could close the [[Eye of Terror]].{{citethis}} 

Cherubael served Quixos for many decades, until finally Quixos himself was slain by Inquisitor Eisenhorn in combat.{{citethis}}

Cherubael had first encountered Inquisitor Eisenhorn while assisting Quixos's accomplice, Inquisitor [[Konrad Molitor]], to secure the [[Necroteuch]]. He engineered his freedom through the manipulation of events surrounding Inquisitor Eisenhorn, making sure that Eisenhorn was in the right place at the right time, with the right weapon, to banish Cherubael back to the Warp and release him from the bonds Quixos had used to enslave him. However, Eisenhorn later ensnared the daemon in a [[daemonhost]] of his own. Later on, a desperate Eisenhorn called upon Cherubael to stop a rampaging [[Chaos Titan]].  The daemon destroyed it, but was bound within the body of a young inquisitor. While Eisenhorn was reluctant to walk the path of the [[Radical]], he used a more controlled form of the daemon, bound by the arcane literature of the [[Malus Codicium]], to defeat [[Pontius Glaw]].{{Fn|3b}} Cherubael was still with Eisenhorn years later, during his brief meeting with his protege, [[Gideon Ravenor]], in a temple of the [[Divine Fratery]].{{Fn|1}} 

Still in the service of Eisenhorn, who has utterly submitted the Daemon thanks to his use of [[Enuncia]], Cherubael expressed his boredom and frequently sought to entertain himself by conversing with the clone of [[Alizebeth Bequin]] in the Inquisitor's service.{{Fn|5a}} Later during the attempts to enter the [[City of Dust]], the domain of the [[King in Yellow]], Eisenhorn dispatched Cherubael to recover Bequin but was stopped by [[Comus]]. The two engaged in a fierce battle.{{Fn|5b}}

Chyron.wikitext:
{{DeathwatchPortal}}
'''Chyron''' is a [[Deathwatch Dreadnought]] belonging to [[Kill-team Talon]].{{Fn|1}}

==History==
A Dreadnought of the [[Lamenters]] Chapter, Chyron did not possess a nickname, but something he ''did'' have was a tremendously foul temper.  Assigned to the Deathwatch before the loss of contact with the Lamenters after they encountered a Tyranid [[Hive Fleet]], Chyron considered himself the last of the Lamenters.  Due to the fate of his Chapter, his attachment to Talon was considered permanent.  When Chyron objected to an order from Sigma to keep a Tyranid life-form that Talon had encountered alive, Sigma threatened the Dreadnought with expulsion from the Deathwatch, and since he had no Chapter to return to, Sigma commented that Chyron would be given to nothingness. Sigma believed such a threat would work as the Deathwatch was all Chyron had left, but he underestimated the Dreadnought's sense of loss and rage and his need to seek vengeance for his lost brothers, which was the only thing that kept him going.  Despite his disagreeable personality and Dreadnought nature oft proving a hinderance and an irritation to the rest of the squad, Talon as a group refused to abandon him during the mission to [[Menatar]], when Chyron chose to disobey the order to keep the aforementioned Tyranid life-form alive.{{Fn|1}}{{Fn|2}}

Cladius Hiero.wikitext:
[[Image:Cladius.jpg|thumb|right|220px|{{PAGENAME}}{{Fn|1}}]]
'''Cladius Hiero''' was a member of the [[Ultramarines]] during the [[Great Crusade]] and [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|1}}

A hero of the [[Great Crusade]] who worked directly under [[Roboute Guilliman]] on at least six separate occasions, Cladius worked as a [[Field Police]] to ensure order amongst his [[Legion]] and their allies such as the [[World Eaters|War Hounds]]. However upon the eruption of the [[Horus Heresy]] and the [[Battle of Calth|Betrayal at Calth]], Hiero assumed the title of [[Overseer]] and was forced to transition into a new darker role as wide swathes of baseline [[Human]]s were conscripted to aid the war effort. Outside of maintaining discipline in battle he also was ever watchful for signs of dissent or traitorious corruption amongst the ranks of the loyalists. He was given authority to make judgement and enact any punishment he deemed fit for such offenses.{{Fn|1}}

Clain Pent.wikitext:
'''Clain Pent''' was a member of the [[Dark Mechanicum]] and one of [[Kelbor-Hal]]'s [[Nine Disciples]] during the [[Horus Heresy]]. He was ranked Pent (fifth) among the Disciples.

Commanding the [[Ark Mechanicus]] ''[[Pent-Ark]]'', Clain Pent oversaw eight direct [[Tech-Priest]] subordinates and consisted of little more than a brain in a jar inside an armored form. During the [[Siege of Terra]] he beached the ''Pent-Ark'' near the Helios Gate of the [[Imperial Palace]] to allow for the construction of siege engines under the protection of its [[Void Shield]]s.{{Fn|1}}

Later during the final stages of the Siege, Clain Pent leads an assault alongside [[Abaddon]] at the head of a great tusked warengine.{{Fn|2}} After the traitor defeat, Pent's great war engine is seen smoldering in flames but there is no sign of the Dark Adeptus.{{Fn|3}}

Cleander von Castellan.wikitext:
{{ImperiumPortal}}
'''Duke Cleander von Castellan''' is a [[Rogue Trader]] who commands [[House von Castellan]],{{Fn|1}} a scion of a wealthy aristocratic family on [[Xarxis Plethis]], and an [[acolyte]] to Inquisitor [[Covenant]].{{Fn|2}} 

==History==
[[Image:CleandervonCastellan.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Duke Cleander von Castellan{{Fn|3}}]]
Having inherited his family's trade license, he sold the family estate to buy a starship and began his career as a [[Merchant Fleet|merchant]]. His travels took him further and further towards the Southern Rim, and he encountered no less than four non-[[Imperial]] worlds, with which he opened exclusive trade negotiations. It was at this point that [[Inquisitor]] [[Covenant]] caught up with him. However the two struck a bargain: in return for not being punished for failing to disclose the whereabouts of these [[xenos]], the Duke signed an agreement pledging himself and his ship to Covenant. As a result, he has answered to the Inquisitor's call on several occasions. It is not honour that motivates von Castellan, for he has little of it. Rather, he fears Inquisitorial reprisals should he prove too disobedient.{{Fn|2}}

The arrangement puts [[House von Castellan]]'s staff and resources at Inquisitor Covenant's command if need be. This includes Duke Cleander's younger sister [[Viola von Castellan]], who serves as the House's [[Rogue Trader Seneschal|Seneschal]].{{Fn|1}}

Clodde.wikitext:
{{AstraMilitarumPortal}}
'''Clodde''' is an [[Ogryn]] with a core of decency and a desire for a better life, who deserted from the [[Astra Militarum]] along with his best mate, the [[Ratling Sniper]] [[Baggit]].{{Fn|1}}
==History==
During Clodde's time in the [[Militarum Auxilla]], he met Baggit. At some point during this time, they took part in the [[Lamentoros Campaign]].{{Fn|3b}} At another unknown point in time, Clodde was given a [[Bone'ead]] upgrade, which would subsequently be damaged with a bullet lodged in the cranial cybernetics. What effect this may have had on the cognitive upgrade is unclear.{{Fn|3a}}

The two now reside in [[Varangantua]]'s [[Dredge]] district, where [[Baggit]]'s greedy eye and loose morals has led them to become thieves. However they have since landed in debt to a savage crime lord{{Fn|1}} and are currently seeking the legendary [[Wraithbone Phoenix]] to pay off their debts and save their lives.{{Fn|2}}

Cocoer.wikitext:
{{TanithPortal}}
{{spoiler|source=The Guns of Tanith (Novel)}}
'''Cocoer''' was a [[Trooper]] of the [[Tanith First and Only]] [[Imperial Guard Regiment]].{{Fn|1a}}


==Biography==
Cocoer was one of the original [[Tanith]] members of the regiment.{{Fn|1a}} In the closing stages of the [[Siege of Vervunhive]], Cocoer was one of thirty Tanith selected personally by [[Colonel-Commissar]] [[Ibram Gaunt]] to take part in [[Operation Heironymo]], the mission to infiltrate [[The Spike]] and assassinate [[Heritor Asphodel]].{{Fn|1b}}

Later, when the Tanith First were deployed on [[Hagia]], they had to defend the [[Shrinehold of Saint Sabbat]] from an [[Infardi]] army. At one point in the battle, Cocoer was badly wounded from shrapnel thrown by an [[AT70 Reaver Battle Tank|AT70 Reaver]] shell that killed [[Filain]] and [[Mazzedo]].{{Fn|2}}

He managed to survive, however, and went on to take part in the regiment's actions on [[Phantine (Planet)|Phantine]].{{Fn|3a}} Most notably, Cocoer was again personally selected for a special mission by Colonel-Commissar Gaunt: [[Operation Larisel]], the mission to infiltrate [[Ouranberg]] and assassinate the leader of the [[Blood Pact]] divisions on Phantine, [[Sagittar Slaith]].{{Fn|3b}} He was assigned to team Larisel 4 under [[Imperial Guard Scout|Scout]]-[[Sergeant (Imperial Guard)|Sergeant]] [[Oan Mkoll|Mkoll]] alongside [[Nour]], [[Rilke]] and the [[Phantine Skyborne|Skyborne Specialist]] [[Arye Babbist|Babbist]].{{Fn|3c}}

Unfortunately, during the approach to [[Ouranberg]], Larisel 4's [[Marauder Bomber|Marauder]] was shot down by the city's air defences with all hands lost{{Fn|3c}}{{Fn|3d}} (save Mkoll, who managed to save himself with his [[grav-chute]]).{{Fn|3e}}

Colaron Vor Artem Lo Bannick.wikitext:
{{ImperialGuardPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' (sometimes known simply as '''Col'''{{Fn|1b}}) is a [[Lieutenant (Imperial Guard)|Lieutenant]] and [[Tank Commander]] of the [[Imperial Guard]]'s [[Paragonian Regiments]].{{Fn|2}}{{Fn|1a}}


==Biography==
===Early Life===
Colaron Bannick was the son of the Chief Auditor of [[Clan Bannick]], one of the [[Noble House|Clan Families]] of the [[sixth moon of Paragon VI]]. In '''395.[[M41]]''', he was betrothed to [[Kaithalar Beyn Lo Turannigen]] as part of an arranged marriage to tie his clan with [[Clan Turannigen]]. However, after Colaron killed his cousin [[Tuparillio]] in a duel, he joined the Guard to save his family disgrace (although his father still disowned him).{{Fn|1c}}{{Fn|1e}}

===Kalidar===
He was part of the Guard's forces sent to fight the [[Ork]]s of [[Waaagh! Gratzdakka]], which had [[Kalidar War|invaded]] the [[Kalidar System]]. He was assigned to the 3rd Company of the [[42nd Paragon Tank Regiment]].{{Fn|1a}}

Initially [[Tank Commander|commanding]] the [[Leman Russ Battle Tank]] ''[[Indomitable Fury]]'', his tank was destroyed on [[Kalidar IV]] in battle with Ork forces on the [[Kostoval Flats]] but in the process held off the greenskin forces long enough for Guard forces to withdraw. For this bravery Colaron was promoted and made Third Gunner of the [[Baneblade]] ''[[Mars Triumphant]]''.{{Fn|1d}}{{Fn|1f}} During the ensuing battles on Kalidar IV, ''Mars Triumphant'' was destroyed but only after taking a [[Gargant]] with it. For this, he was promoted and given command of a new Baneblade, ''[[Cortein's Honour]]''.{{Fn|1g}}

===Geratomro===
Bannick and his crew were next deployed along with the ''[[Cortein's Honour]]'' to the world of [[Geratomro]], which had risen in rebellion to the Imperium over the issue of the [[Tithe]]. During a chaotic landing Bannick was forced to take command after their commanding officer, [[Kandar Vor Ostrakhan Lo Hannick]], was injured.{{Fn|2a}} The Imperial forces quickly overran the capital of [[Matua Superior]] then conducted a brutal public execution of the rebel leaders.{{Fn|2b}} After a brawl with rival [[Atraxian Regiments|Atraxian]] soldiers at a bar, Bannick and his crew faced punishment but thanks to the sacrifice of his loader, [[Gollph]], only the latter was flogged.{{Fn|2c}}

In further battles with the Geratomran rebels, ''Cortein's Honour'' spearheaded the assault on Yellow Guard Ridge, where it took out a [[Destroyer Tank Hunter]].{{Fn|2d}} By this point, a full-scale [[Chaos]] invasion had erupted across Geratomro thanks to the machinations of the [[Daemonic Herald]] [[Dib]]. ''Cortein's Honour'' was then ambushed by [[Chaos Space Marine]] [[Predator]]s. Amid the chaos, ''Cortein's Honour'' was badly damaged and Bannick and his crew were assigned to the [[Shadowsword]] ''[[Lux Imperator]]''.{{Fn|2e}} In a battle against [[Chaos Titan]]s, the ''Lux Imperator'' was severely damaged but managed to delivered the decisive blow to a [[Chaos Warlord Titan|Warlord]].{{Fn|2f}}

Shortly after crippling the Titan, Bannick and his crew were badly wounded after the ''Lux Imperator'' was hit by the [[Emperor's Children]]. The sudden arrival of [[Black Templars]] forces saved his crew.{{Fn|2g}} Led by the [[Space Marine]]s, Bannick and the ''Lux Imperator'' fought through the [[Daemon]]-infested streets of Geratomro. Thanks to the sacrifice of the [[Emperor's Champion]] [[Bastoigne]], the [[Warp Rift]] the Chaos forces used to invade Geratomro was weakened enough to allow for the ''Lux Imperator'' to destroy it.{{Fn|2h}} 

In the aftermath of the battle, Bannick and his crew faced a possible purge by the [[Commissariat]] for their exposure to Chaos. The revelation caused his driver, [[Karlok Shoam]], to kill the Commissar on board their tank while Bannick was forced to execute [[Lieutenant (Imperial Guard)|Lieutenant]] [[Epperaliant]] when he refused to lie about what had transpired. Bannick then watched as much of Geratomro was purged to hide the truth of Chaos.{{Fn|2h}}

Constantin Valdor.wikitext:
{{ambig|subject=Chief Custodian|disambiguation=Valdor}} {{Character |Portal ={{AdeptusCustodesPortal}} |Name ={{PAGENAME}} |Image =ValdorHH.jpg |Caption =Constantin Valdor{{Fn|7}} |Title =The [[Emperor]]'s Spear
First of the Ten Thousand |Homeworld =[[Terra]] |Birth =[[Age of Strife]], [[Terra]]{{Fn|13c}} |Active Period =[[M29]] - ??? |Death = |Cause of Death = |Species =[[Human]] |Type =[[Custodes]] |Gender =Male |Relatives ='' *Unnamed Parents{{Fn|13c}} |Occupation ='' *[[Captain-General]] of the [[Adeptus Custodes|Legio Custiodes]]
(Formerly) |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction = '' '' *[[Imperium of Man]] **[[Legio Custodes]] |Notes = }} '''Constantin Valdor''' ('Emperor's Spear'), the '''First of the Ten Thousand'''{{Fn|6c}}, was the Chief Custodian to the [[Emperor of Mankind]] as [[Captain-General]] of the [[Adeptus Custodes]] at the time of the [[Unification Wars]], [[Great Crusade]], and the [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|5}} ==Biography== ===Unification Wars=== [[Image:Constantin Valdor.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Chief-Custodian {{PAGENAME}}{{Fn|2}}]] The origins of Constantin Valdor are mysterious. According to [[Amar Astarte]], his original parents were killed by the [[Emperor]], who moved entire armies across continents to locate and retrieve him. Valdor himself knows very little of his past before becoming the Emperor's servant.{{Fn|13c}} While commonly accepted as the first Custodes, Valdor does not recall if he was truly the first Custodian, or simply the first successfully produced one.{{Fn|10}} He served during the [[Unification Wars]] at the [[Battle of Maulland Sen]]. A handful of years later, he assassinated [[Koja Zu]], the Minister of the Anuatan Steppes{{Fn|6a}}, and claimed her son, [[Ra Endymion]]{{Fn|6d}}, for the Legio Custodes.{{Fn|6b}} During the [[Battle of Maulland Sen]], Valdor witnessed the savagery of the [[Thunder Warriors]] and became worried over their future.{{Fn|13b}} By the end of the [[Unification Wars]] Valdor had emerged as part of the ruling "triumvirate" of Terra alongside the Emperor and Malcador. He had become suspicious of [[Grand Provost Marshal]] [[Uwoma Kandawire]], dispatching [[Samonas]] to unravel her conspiracy before it could begin.{{Fn|13a}} However the conspirators still struck in the [[Palace Coup]], during which Valdor was confronted by Kandawire, as well as [[Ushotan]] and his surviving [[Thunder Warrior]]s. Valdor urged the conspirators to surrender, but when they refused he deployed the proto-[[Legiones Astartes]] in their first battle. During the battle the rebels were crushed and Valdor slew Ushotan, an act he took no gratification in as he had admired the General. Surprisingly, Valdor spared Kandawire and let her leave the Palace to retire in peace.{{Fn|13d}}{{Fn|13e}} Later Valdor expressed his surprise when Malcador stated that the Primarchs were still alive and that the Emperor was attempting to find them. Valdor couldn't understand why the [[Chaos|Arch-Enemy]] had decided to spare them, and believed that if they were alive then they would be corrupted. Valdor instead wished to raise armies of mortals to be led by his Custodians.{{Fn|13f}} Prior to the Horus Heresy, Valdor had [[Adeptus Custodes#Outlook and training|earned]] 1932 names.{{Fn|3}} By the [[41st Millennium]] a book which apparently had his whole name written down took up an entire volume.{{Fn|15}} ===Horus Heresy=== [[Image:Hh valdor-closeup.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Constantin Valdor{{Fn|20}}]] ====Battle of Prospero==== Just prior to the open outbreak of the [[Horus Heresy]], Valdor was charged by the Emperor to accompany [[Leman Russ (primarch)|Leman Russ]] of the [[Space Wolves]] in bringing [[Magnus the Red]] to account for breaking promises made during the [[Council of Nikaea]] at which the Emperor strictly forbade the use of sorcery and psychic powers.{{Fn|2}} Valdor, with a contingent of elite Custodian Guard, fought alongside Russ and the Space Wolves on [[Battle of Prospero|Prospero]]. He and his forces were responsible for killing at least three of the greatest psykers of the [[Thousand Sons]] and routing a force much more numerous than their own, however little else is known after this. Valdor eventually faced over thirty of the elite [[Khenetai]] "Blademasters", warriors who could predict an enemies' attacks through psychic precognition. The Captain-General slew every one of these deadly warriors, receiving only a single wound in the process. According to one account, he was also responsible for saving [[Bjorn]] when his arm was corrupted by the sorcerous powers of a Thousand Sons psyker. Valdor sliced Bjorn's arm off to prevent the corruption from overrunning his body. The other states that Bjorn's arm was cut off by a Skjald of the Space Wolves, [[Kasper Ansbach Hawser|Kasper Hawser]].{{Fn|2}}{{Fn|4}} ====Later Actions==== [[File:ValdorArtNovel.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Constantin Valdor in the [[Imperial Palace]].{{Fn|20}}]] When [[Amon Tauromachian]] returned from his extended [[Blood Game]], Valdor informed his fellow Custodian of how [[Horus|Horus Lupercal]] had declared [[Horus Heresy|rebellion]] against the Emperor. When Tauromachian asked how this could happen, Valdor, speaking as someone who knew the [[Warmaster]], rejected theories that it was pride or resentment, instead voicing his belief that [[Chaos|something]] had driven Horus and his closest advisers mad. Valdor then assigned Tauromachian with the task of investigating [[Pherom Sichar]], Lord of [[Hy Brasil]], for evidence of treason.{{Fn|3}} After Horus declared his rebellion, Valdor then oversaw the mission and deployment of the first ever execution team. Invited by the [[Master of Assassins]] whose secret identity was [[Malcador The Sigillite]] who oversaw the council of Assassins. Each clade- [[Venenum]], [[Eversor]], [[Culexus]], [[Vanus]], [[Callidus]], and led by [[Vindicare]] selected a single alpha-dan operative for the mission. The target was [[Horus Lupercal]]. [[Rogal Dorn]] learned of such events and challenged Valdor claiming that Horus being alive was a boon because he was predictable, and killing the head of the rebellion would not stop it, someone more predictable would simply take over. Valdor argued that the actions of the [[Officio Assassinorum]] were not necessarily cowardly, but expedient. Valdor says to Dorn that they all want the same thing; to preserve the Emperor. Dorn however claims that Valdor's role is to safeguard the life of the Emperor, whilst Dorn himself, and all the [[Astartes]] role is to safeguard the [[Imperium]]. The Assassin's mission uncovered valuable information, and encountered [[Erebus]]' own agent, daemonically enhanced. The mission to kill [[Horus]] is a failure as Horus is tipped off of the attempt on his life and sends a proxy who is killed in his place. Dorn and Valdor continue to argue, Dorn citing that to preserve the Imperium we must have a moral code, Valdor citing that to match Horus' evil we must not stop at underhanded tactics. The [[Emperor]] settles the argument with the final statement ''"No more shadows. No more veils"''. {{Fn|1}} Later as the majority of the Custodian Guard was occupied by the [[War Within the Webway]], Valdor assumed a vital position on the loyalist [[War Council]] alongside Malcador, Rogal Dorn, and [[Kane]].{{Fn|6c}} He reappeared shortly before [[Leman Russ (Primarch)|Leman Russ]] left Terra to confront Horus directly, returning the [[Spear of Russ]] to him. During their conservation, Valdor expressed disdain at the [[Space Wolves]] use of [[Rune Priest]]s, considering them no different from normal [[Librarian]]s which were now banned due to the [[Council of Nikaea]].{{Fn|9}} Valdor next appeared as the [[Solar War]] began, meeting with Rogal Dorn alongside [[Sanguinius]], [[Jaghatai Khan]], Malcador, and Dorn's command staff.{{Fn|11}} ====Siege of Terra==== [[File:HH trailer Valdor.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Constantin Valdor in the [[Imperial Palace]].{{Fn|20}}]] Valdor fought in defence of Mankind's homeworld during the [[Siege of Terra]]. During the battle loyalist marines who witnessed the Captain-General in combat, saw him reave through traitor marines as easily as they would against ordinary humans and weaker xenos. He also deployed [[Amon Tauromachian]] to investigate apparent [[Daemonic]] activity in the [[Imperial Palace]]. When Amon asked what should be done to [[Euphrati Keeler]] and her proto-[[Imperial Cult]]ists, Valdor ordered that they remain unharmed as part of Malcador's plan to use them in the fight against Chaos.{{Fn|12b}} After the fall of the [[Lion's Gate Spaceport]] he helped lead the defense of the [[Colossi Gate]] alongside Jaghatai Khan and Raldoron, fighting against swathes of [[Daemons]].{{Fn|14}} After the escape of [[Basilio Fo]] from [[Blackstone Prison]] Valdor saw the mad scientist a threat big enough to warrant his own personal attention, and he hunted the prisoner throughout the Palace.{{Fn|19a}} He eventually saved Fo from a roaming [[Night Lord]] and decided that the human's supposed anti-Astartes bio-weapon could be of service to the Emperor.{{Fn|19b}} Valdor was summoned to the Emperor's side during the final teleportation attack aboard the ''[[Vengeful Spirit]]'', and he left Basillo Fo and his weapon in the hands of his own Custodes.{{Fn|17a}} During the battle aboard the ''Vengful Spirit'' Valdor became separated from the Emperor and he and his Custodes found themselves in a dark abyss surrounded by [[Daemon]]s. Part of a trap by Horus to drive the Captain-General to torment, it made him feel something close to fear for the first time as he realized he could not fulfil his duty. Nonetheless, this did not stop Valdor's killing duty in the slightest as he slaughtered his way through hordes of Daemons. To confirm that he had indeed been teleported to the ''Vengeful Spirit'', Valdor plunged the [[Apollonian Spear]] into its floor to reveal its identity.{{Fn|17b}} Valdor's forces continued to battle through madness and Daemons until he grew closer to the location of the [[Emperor]], at which point he began to encounter [[Sons of Horus]] and [[Word Bearers]] for the first time. During the struggle, he spotted [[First Captain]] [[Abaddon]].{{Fn|18}} [[Image:SycarValdor.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Impaled by a [[Power Sword]], Valdor battles [[Hellas Sycar]] and other [[Justaerin]] aboard the ''[[Vengeful Spirit]]''{{Fn|19a}}]] Injured and weakened from their previous battles, Valdor and his remaining Custodes fought admirably against a vicious counterattack launched by Abaddon consisting of [[Justaerin]] and veteran [[Word Bearers]], who outnumbered them by over thirty to one. However, the traitor Astartes were aided by [[Erebus]], who managed to greatly empower Abaddon through Warp-infused rituals. During the fighting, Valdor was pinned down by six Justaerin Terminators and badly wounded by [[Hellas Sycar]], but kept on fighting and managed to cut Abaddon with the [[Apollonian Spear]]. Gaining insight from Abaddon's future, Valdor was horrified to see the next 10,000 years of war and labeled Abaddon "Despoiler" before punching him.{{Fn|19a}} The experience, as well as the sudden berserk frenzy of the [[Blood Angels]] contingent of Operation Anabasis, left Valdor unsettled and angry, and afterwards he displayed more brutal and impatient traits, particularly towards Dorn and the Astartes whom he repeatedly spouted curses towards. However, he also learned of Sanguinius' death, something which caused Valdor genuine grief. Valdor and Dorn were ultimately able to escape Abaddon's attack and finally make it to [[Lupercal's Court]].{{Fn|19b}} Within Lupercal's Court, Valdor and Dorn discovered [[Garviel Loken]] and [[Leetu]] as the only survivors alongside the corpse of Horus and the grievously wounded Emperor. Seeing the state of the Emperor made Valdor, Coros, and the other surviving Custodes weep. Leetu discovered a [[Imperial Tarot|tarot card]] of "The Throne", which helped Dorn argue that the Emperor should be brought back to the Golden Throne. Valdor initially dismissed the superstition, but ultimately acquiesced.{{Fn|19c}} After the Siege of Terra, Valdor met with the newly arrived Leman Russ. While Russ was distraught and pessimistic about what had befallen the Imperium and Emperor, Valdor expressed confidence that the Master of Mankind had foreseen all that had transpired and planned accordingly. Secretly, however, Valdor is unsure if this is true.{{Fn|10}} ===Fate=== Sometime after the Heresy, around the same time as the disappearance of [[Leman Russ (Primarch)|Leman Russ]], Valdor also disappeared without a trace. During the dead of night, Valdor simply slipped out of the Imperial Palace, turning back once to look upon the Palace and whisper ''"Only in Death"'' (the first part of the Imperial quote ''Only in death does duty end'') before vanishing.{{Fn|10}} His fate is unknown even by the Custodes themselves. He is one of three Captains-General to have gone missing without even the Adeptus Custodes being aware of the details.{{Fn|8}} A book recovered and translated by [[Gideon Ravenor]] and [[Alizebeth Bequin]] identified the enigmatic [[King in Yellow]] as apparently being Constantin Valdor.{{Fn|15}} ==Personality and Abilities== Beyond his absolute loyalty to the Emperor, Constantin Valdor was known for his stoic and observant personality.{{Fn|10}} Despite the claims by outside observers he did not experience emotions such as pride or arrogance, or really any feeling at all besides his sense of duty to the Emperor. The [[Thunder Warrior]] [[Ushotan]] expressed pity for Valdor, stating that he had all the humanity sucked from him and had become numb. Valdor did not disagree with the sentiment.{{Fn|13d}}{{Fn|13e}} Nonetheless he seemed capable of taking fondness to certain individuals, such as [[Uwoma Kandawire]] and Ushotan.{{Fn|13f}} Valdor's battle prowess was legendary. His reaction time was to the point where it seemed as if he could see time itself come to a halt.{{Fn|13d}}{{Fn|13e}} A warrior of superlative skill, it was said that Valdor could match even a [[Primarch]] in single combat. Indeed, such was his might, that there were those, even in the Imperial Court, who called him a "Primarch" in all but name.{{Fn|6e}} ==Wargear== Valdor went into battle equipped with a expertly crafted [[Guardian Spear]] known as the [[Apollonian Spear]] and an ornate suit of [[Custodian Armour]] known as the [[Corinthine Warplate]].{{Fn|7}} ==Related Videos== {{#evt: service=youtube |id=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NsUTzk5wUM4 |alignment=center |container=frame }} ==Images== [[Image:ValdorMini.jpg|thumb|center|250px|Constantin Valdor Miniature]] ==Sources== {{Cite}} *{{Endn|1}}: [[Nemesis (Novel)]], {{Cite This}} *{{Endn|2}}: [[Horus Heresy: Collected Visions]], pgs. 236–241 *{{Endn|3}}: [[Blood Games (Short Story)]] *{{Endn|4}}: [[Prospero Burns (Novel)]],{{Cite this}} *{{Endn|5}}: [[Imperial Armour Volume One - Corbulo.wikitext:
{{Character |Portal ={{BloodAngelsPortal}} |Name =Corbulo |Image =CorbuloArt.jpg |Caption =Corbulo{{Fn|4}} |Title = |Homeworld =[[Baal]] |Birth = |Active Period =[[M41]] - Present |Death = |Cause of Death = |Species =[[Human]] |Type =[[Astartes]] |Gender =Male |Relatives =[[Sanguinius]]
("Father" via [[Gene-Seed]]) |Occupation =[[Sanguinary High Priest]] of the [[Blood Angels]] |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Imperium of Man]] **[[Blood Angels]] |Notes = }} '''Corbulo''' is the [[Sanguinary High Priest]] of the [[Blood Angels]]. ===Biography=== It is his duty to guard the [[Red Grail]], the holy cup which was used to preserve the blood of [[Sanguinius]] after he was slain. It is from this cup that the assembled Sanguinary Priests drink as part of the ritual of initiating a new [[Sanguinary Priest]].{{Fn|1}} Corbulo resembles the [[Primarch]] of the Blood Angels, [[Sanguinius]] both physically and spiritually. He has become determined to cure the Blood Angels and their successors of the [[Red Thirst]], a quest that has taken him across the galaxy in search of wonders from the [[Dark Age of Technology]]. In addition, he shares Sanginius's foresight and has limited abilities in [[Divination]]. However while this gift is sometimes used to the Chapter's advantage in battle, he is most focused on researching a cure to his chapter's affliction. Nonetheless, his skills have been put to good use by the Chapter in other fields. The reason the Blood Angels arrived so quickly to counter the [[Second War for Armageddon]] by the [[Ork]] [[Ghazghkull]] was due to his divination. Similarly, without his guidance the Blood Angels fleet would not have known the location of [[M'kar the Reborn]]'s [[Daemonship]] as it entered the [[Baal]] system, perhaps saving the planet from destruction.{{Fn|1}} It is also said that Corbulo was able to forewarn the chapter of the coming [[Tyranid]] [[Devastation of Baal|assault on Baal]].{{Fn|5}} However these successes have not come without cost, for Corbulo has become more withdrawn, with some suspecting that he has foreseen a grave future for the Blood Angels.{{Fn|1}} ====Defence of Baal==== Corbulo was present on [[Baal]] after the [[Arkio]] Insurrection. He participated in the council, along with [[Commander Dante]] and [[Chief Librarian]] [[Mephiston]], when Dante decided to call a conclave of the Angels' [[Successor Chapter]]s.{{Fn|2b}} One of his subordinate [[Sanguinary Priest]]s, [[Caecus]], proposed the radical solution of using [[replicae]] (cloning) techniques to replace the Angels' losses, but Dante disapproved of the plan.{{Fn|2x}} When [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] [[Rydae]] of the [[Angels Sanguine]] was accidentally killed by Caecus, Corbulo began to examine him, but [[Chapter Master]] [[Sentikan]] held him back, preventing the dead Captain's helmet from being removed.{{Fn|2c}} During the surprise attack by the [[Bloodfiend]]s on the chapel of the [[Red Grail]], Corbulo tried to stop their leader, the ''alpha'', but was knocked aside and could not stop the fiend from draining its contents down its throat. He was, however, able to save the Grail from being stolen.{{Fn|2d}} Later, he fought alongside Dante and the other Space Marines when the Bloodfiends assaulted the Holy Sepulchre where [[Sanguinius]]'s remains were interred.{{Fn|2e}} ====Recent Actions==== Fascinated by the newly induced [[Primaris Space Marine]]s, or more specifically their potential resistance to the [[Red Thirst]] and [[Black Rage]], Corbulo made it his business to accompany them into battle wherever he could. However he became disappointed with the results following the [[Khovan Incident]].{{Fn|3}} ===Wargear=== Armed with a standard issue [[Bolt pistol]] and a relic [[Chainsword]] named [[Heaven's Teeth]], Corbulo also carries an [[Exsanguinator]] and the [[Red Grail]], which not only inspires other Blood Angels to greater acts of valour but also generates a powerful [[force field]].{{Fn|1}} ===Images=== [[Image:Corbulo.jpg|thumb|center|220px|High Priest Corbulo]] ===Sources=== *{{Endn|1}}: [[Codex: Blood Angels (5th Edition)]], pg. 49 *{{Endn|2}}: [[Red Fury (Novel)] **{{Endn|2a}}: {{Cite This}}, pg. 58 **{{Endn|2b}}: {{Cite This}}, pg. 88 **{{Endn|2c}}: {{Cite This}}, pg. 179 **{{Endn|2d}}: {{Cite This}}, pg. 228 **{{Endn|2e}}: {{Cite This}}, pg. 250 **{{Endn|2x}}: {{Cite This}} *{{Endn|3}}: [[Codex: Blood Angels (8th Edition)]], pg. 22 *{{Endn|4}}: [[Shield of Baal: Exterminatus]] — ''Cathedral in the Clouds'' *{{Endn|5}}: [[Codex: Blood Angels (9th Edition)]], pg. 9 ====Uncited==== *[[Codex: Blood Angels (4th Edition)]], pg. 8 *[[Codex: Blood Angels (3rd Edition)]], {{Cite This}} *[[Codex: Angels of Death (2nd Edition)]], {{Cite This}} {{BAForces}} [[Category:Blood Angels (Novel Series)]] [[Category:Characters (Blood Angels)]] [[Category:Characters (Space Marine Apothecaries)]] [[de:Corbulo]] [[fr:Corbulo]]

[[Venerable Dreadnought|Venerable-Praefectus]] '''Coriolanus, Archon of Stone,''' was a [[Leviathan Dreadnought]] in the [[Dark Angels]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]], during the [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|1}}

He served the [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]] for more than two centuries, and was once the Marshal of the [[Host of Stone]], before his internment within a [[Space Marine Dreadnought|Dreadnought]]. As the [[Horus Heresy]] raged, Coriolanus took part in the [[Thramas Crusade]] and was among the [[Dark Angels]] that defended [[Nadress III]] from the [[Night Lords]]. His Legion's might was not enough to save the world, though, and the fortress Coriolanus was defending began to be overwhelmed by the Traitors. Before it fell to the Night Lords, however, Coriolanus sacrificed himself, by using his [[Leviathan Dreadnought|Leviathan]]'s [[Grav-flux bombard]] to collapse the fortress around him, entombing them all in rubble.{{Fn|1}}

Cornelius von Ravensburg.wikitext:
{{ImperialNavyPortal}}
{{ambig|subject=Imperial Navy admiral|disambiguation=Cornelius}}
'''Cornelius von Ravensburg''' was a [[Lord Admiral]] in the [[Imperial Navy]], who took part in the [[Gothic War]].{{Fn|1b}}
==History==
[[Image:Ravensburg.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Admiral Ravensburg{{Fn|1a}}]]
The commander of the [[Battlefleet]] of the [[Gothic Sector]] during the [[12th Black Crusade]], von Ravensburg was the chief [[Imperial]] commander in what would later become known as the [[Gothic War]].{{Fn|1b}} Overseeing Imperial naval forces from the opening [[Chaos]] surprise attack to the very end of the conflict, von Ravensburg had to juggle not only the incursion by [[Abaddon the Despoiler]] but also [[Eldar Corsair|Eldar Corsairs]], [[Ork]] raiders, and [[Human]] [[pirate]]s.{{Fn|1c}} von Ravensburg's most famous action was the [[Battle of Gethsemane]], the engagement which turned the tide of the Gothic War in favor of the Imperium.{{Fn|1d}} After Imperial forces finally emerged victorious in the conflict, von Ravensburg was honoured by the [[High Lords of Terra]] by having a monolith which had his name inscribed upon it constructed in the honour of those who fought in the Gothic War.{{Fn|1e}}

Left for dead on a devastated planet, Corpulax awoke as a reanimated corpse. However, unlike so many of the plague’s victims, Corpulax retained his intelligence and cognitive powers. (I Legion) |Notes = }} '''Corswain''', the '''Hound of Caliban''', was a [[Lord Commander (Legiones Astartes)|Lord Commander]]{{fn|14a}} and the Captain-[[Paladin (Dark Angels)|Paladin]] of the [[Dark Angels]]' 9th Order during the [[Great Crusade]] and [[Horus Heresy]], later commanding half the [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]] as [[Lion El'Jonson|The Lion's]] Seneschal.{{fn|3}} ===Biography=== Corswain was born on [[Caliban]] but was not inducted into [[The Order]]. He was uniquely placed to bridge the divisions within the First Legion during its formation into the Dark Angels under [[Lion El'Jonson]]'s leadership. He was groomed to serve not any one Host or Order but to command the respect and knowledge of all.{{Fn|8}} Corswain became the Paladin of the 9th Order under [[Praetor (Rank)|Master]] [[Alajos]] during the [[Great Crusade]]. The finest swordsman in the Legion, he was the bearer of the Mantle of the Champion and one of only two Dark Angels ever to best Alajos.{{Fn|1}} In time his reputation grew similar to the likes of [[Raldoron]] and [[Sigismund]].{{Fn|8}} He was among the forces of the 9th Order that stripped [[Luther]] of his ships after he disobeyed his orders to remain on [[Caliban]] in order to aid [[Horus]] at [[Zaramund]] in 970.[[M30]].{{Fn|3}} ====Horus Heresy==== After the outbreak of the [[Horus Heresy]], Corswain fought alongside his [[Primarch]] [[Lion El'Jonson]] against the [[Night Lords]] in the [[Thramas Crusade]]. On [[Tsagualsa]], Corswain and Alajos accompanied the Lion when he met with the Primarch of the Night Lords [[Konrad Curze]] and his own [[Honour Guard]]. After battle broke out between the two sides, Corswain and Alajos battled [[Sevatar]] and [[Shang]]. Corswain was unable to prevent Captain Alajos from being killed, but impaled Curze as he strangled the Lion - leaving the sword in the primarch's spine.{{Fn|1}} Two years into the Thramas Crusade, Corswain was made Seneschal{{Fn|2}} and, after the [[Battle of Perditus]], given command of half of the remaining Legion to with hunt down and eliminate [[First Captain]] [[Calas Typhon]] and his [[Death Guard]] splinter fleet while the Lion travelled with the other half to [[Ultramar]]. Sustaining heavy casualties at the hands of the Death Guard, Corswain sent a small number of volunteers to Caliban with transports to bring reinforcement.{{Fn|3}} However these reinforcements never arrived, angering Corswain. He eventually rendezvoused with Luther and his secretly [[Fallen]] warriors at [[Zaramund]], unaware that Luther had [[Second Zaramund Campaign|just secured the system for himself]]. Luther had fully committed himself to independence from the Imperium, and was secretly harboring the fleet of [[Death Guard]] which Corswain was pursuing. Luther deceived Corswain, stating that they had driven off the Death Guard. Corswain scolded Luther for violating the Lion's edict to not leave Caliban but otherwise fell for the ploy.{{Fn|11b}} [[File:CorswainArt.jpg|thumb|right|Corswain{{Fn|10}}]] Corswain next appeared during the [[Siege of Terra]], arriving at the edge of the [[Sol System]] to rendezvous with [[Admiral]] [[Niora Su-Kassen]] and the ''[[Phalanx]]'' and proclaimed his forces were ready to fight for the [[Emperor]].{{Fn|7}} Hiding at the edges of the Sol System, Corswain convinced Su-Kassen to a plan to have him and his warriors land on Terra to take part in the battle.{{Fn|12a}} Using the ''[[Imperator Somnium]]'', Corswain was able to break the traitor blockade and land on the [[Forbidden Fortress|Hollow Mountain]].{{Fn|12b}} The Dark Angels found the complex occupied by the forces of [[Chaos]], and he was nearly overcome by the [[Daemon]] [[Vassukella]].{{Fn|12c}} Saved by [[Vassago]], Corswain expressed his intent to reactivate the [[Astronomican]].{{Fn|12d}} In the final hours of the Siege, Corswain was horrified to learn of the murder of [[Vassago]] but faced more pressing matters as the [[Death Guard]] under [[Typhus]] moved in to retake the Astronomican. Despite being vastly outnumbered, Corswain slew a hulking [[Plague Marine]] but was wounded. He was steadied by [[Zahariel El'Zurias]], who had taken the mantle of the [[Lord Cypher]].{{Fn|14b}} In the subsequent battle, the Dark Angels were nearly overwhelmed by Typhus and the Death Guard but Corswain was committed to using Cypher's psychic talents to reactivate the Astronomican and guide [[Guilliman]]'s fleet to Terra.{{Fn|15}} Alongside [[Sigismund]], Corswain led the defence of the [[Hollow Mountain]], coming into personal conflict with [[Typhus]]. All seemed lost until [[Euphrati Keeler]] and her followers were able to reactivate the Astronomican, throwing back the traitors and giving the location of Terra to [[Guilliman]]'s fleet of reinforcements.{{Fn|16}} ====Return to Caliban==== Corswain survived the Heresy to return to Caliban. During the [[Destruction of Caliban]], he was among the first to make planetfall and do battle with the [[Fallen]].{{Fn|4}} During the battle, Corswain cornered and duelled the [[Zahariel El'Zurias|Lord Cypher]].{{Fn|11a}} ====Legacy==== Corswain is a legendary figure to the Dark Angels of the [[M41|41st Millennium]]. The sword he wielded during the fall of Caliban is known as the [[Blade of Corswain]], presented as the bladesman's honour to the finest swordsman in the [[Ravenwing]].{{Fn|5}} He also lends his name to the [[Lost Mace of Corswain]], a relic power maul used by the Deathwing.{{Fn|6}} ===Wargear=== *[[The Blade (Dark Angels)|The Blade]] *[[Armour of the Forest]] *[[Mantle of the Champion]] ===Images=== CorswainMini.jpg|Corswain miniature{{Fn|13}} ===Sources=== {{Cite}} *{{Endn|1}}: [[Savage Weapons (Short Story)]] *{{Endn|2}}: [[The Lion (Novella)]], ''I'' *{{Endn|3}}: [[Angels of Caliban (Novel)]], Fifteen *{{Endn|4}}: [[Holder of the Keys (Audio Drama)]] *{{Endn|5}}: [[Ravenwing (Novel)]], ''Honour'' *{{Endn|6}}: [[Space Hulk: Deathwing]] *{{Endn|7}}: [[Saturnine (Novel)]], Epilogue *{{Endn|8}}: [[The Horus Heresy Book Nine - Crusade]], pg. 170 *{{Endn|9}}: [[The Horus Heresy: Legions]] *{{Endn|10}}: [https://siegeofterra.com/ Siegeofterra.com: Mortis section] (last accessed 3/17/2021) *11: [[Luther: First of the Fallen (Novel)]]: **{{Endn|11a}}: ''Tale of the Lion'' **{{Endn|11b}}: ''Tale of the Traitor'' *12: [[Mortis (Novel)]]: **{{Endn|12a}}: Chapter 5 **{{Endn|12b}}: Chapter 12 **{{Endn|12c}}: Chapter 16 **{{Endn|12d}}: Chapter 22 *{{Endn|13}}: [https://www.warhammer-community.com/2022/10/06/heresy-thursday-an-illustrious-dark-angel-joins-the-civil-war/ Warhammer Community: Heresy Thursday – An Illustrious Dark Angel Joins the Civil War (posted 6/10/2022)] ''(last accessed 9/10/2022)'' *14:[[The End and the Death: Volume I (Novel)]]: **{{Endn|14a}}: 2:i **{{Endn|14b}}: 3:xxiii *{{Endn|15}}: [[The End and the Death: Volume II (Novel)]] - 7:xxxii *{{Endn|16}}: [[The End and the Death: Volume III (Novel)]] - 10:xv [[Category:Characters (Born: Caliban)]] [[Category:Characters (Dark Angels)]] [[Category:Characters (Horus Heresy)]] [[fr:Corswain]]

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[Daemon Prince]] of [[Nurgle]]. He is known as the hope in people's hearts, subverting their faith in order to bring about despair.{{Fn|2b}}

Called forth during the [[Horus Heresy]] by the dark rites of the traitorous [[Word Bearers]] [[Legion]], the [[Ruinstorm]] unleashed a vast horde of the malevolent denizens of the Warp upon the [[Imperium]]. Most deadly amongst them were those that came to be known as the Daemon Princes of the Ruinstorm, and counted amongst their number was the vile, pestilent and ever-hungry Cor’bax Utterblight.

Those who have witnessed this loathsome disciple of [[Nurgle]] in action tell of a tidal wave of rot and disease which spills before Cor’bax as he enters the battlefield. Life corrupts at his touch, and any mortals unfortunate enough to survive are snapped up whole within his gaping maw to slowly perish and fuel the gifts of Nurgle Cor’bax will generously bestow upon the next world he attacks.{{Fn|1}}

During the [[Siege of Terra]] Utterblight was summoned by [[Typhus]] and [[Zardu Layak]] in order to subvert the proto-[[Imperial Cult]] within the [[Imperial Palace]].{{Fn|2b}} He was later summoned inside the [[Sanctum Imperialis]] due to the ignorance of [[Euphrati Keeler]]'s followers, only defeated thanks to the efforts of the [[Custodes]] [[Amon Tauromachian]].{{Fn|2a}}

Costalis.wikitext:
{{ImperiumPortal}}
'''Costalis''' was the [[Planetary Governor]] of the [[Ultramar]] world [[Iax]], during the last years of the [[Plague Wars]] and he ruled from its capital city '''First Landing'''.{{Fn|1a}}

==Biography==
{{Spoiler|source= Dark Imperium: Godblight (Novel)}}
His world suffered greatly at the [[Death Guard]]'s hands and it began to be rotted out by the diseases of the [[Chaos God]] [[Nurgle]]. Like many of [[Iax]]'s population, Costalis became sickened and became so physically weak, that he was forced to be moved around in a wheelchair. When [[Lord Commander]] [[Guilliman]] later arrived with his forces, to defeat the Death Guard's [[Daemon Primarch]] [[Mortarion]] and free Iax, the [[Planetary Governor]] stood from his wheelchair to greet the [[Primarch]]. As Guilliman approached him, Costalis got to one knee and said it was an honor to meet the Lord Commander. He would go on to offer his apologies for the poor state that Iax was in, despite it being considered the most beautiful of [[Ultramar]]'s worlds. Guilliman told him to rise in response, but the Lord Commander had to help the Governor as Costalis struggled to get up. After seeing Costalis' deteriorated condition, Guilliman helped him into the wheelchair and ordered Governor to go be treated at a medicae. Costalis agreed and Guilliman told him to rest afterwards, until the Lord Commander was ready to unveil how they would defeat the Death Guard. As the Planetary Governor was wheeled away, however, the [[Adeptus Custodes]] [[Actuarius Maldovar Colquan|Colquan]], who had accompanied Guilliman, remarked that Costalis was fatally sick and had seen his last days.{{Fn|1a}}  

[[Guilliman]] later revealed his battle plans, during the meeting and explained that '''First Landing'''' would be used as his forces' base of operation. Costalis, though, was quick to explain that while the [[Death Guard]] held most of [[Iax]], there were other areas still held by his population. They would also need the [[Lord Commander]]'s protection if they were to survive the coming battle. Guilliman assured the [[Planetary Governor]], that he would deploy a portion of his forces to protect these areas as well. However, the Death Guard would likely target First Landing and its people would not survive if that occurred. To the shock of many of the city's defenders, the Lord Commander stated that, regardless of their rank, the city's population would be evacuated to his fleet in Iax's orbit.{{Fn|1b}} While Guilliman was later successful in defeating the Death Guard, Iax was left heavily corrupted by their invasion. In order to save as much of the world as he could, the Lord Commander then ordered Iax's tainted areas to be cleansed by atomic weaponry. Because of this, it is not known if Costalis will live long enough to be able to safely return to Iax.{{Fn|1c}}

[[Inquisitor]] '''Covenant''' is an [[Ordo Malleus]] [[Inquisitor]] and a [[psyker]], who possesses limited psychic abilities. As part of those Inquisitors who have made it their duty to purge the [[Inquisition]] itself of perceived corruption, he is particularly focused in his Inquisitorial duties, especially on destroying the [[Daemonhost]]s created by the more [[Radical]] Inquisitors of the Ordo Malleus.{{Fn|1a}}

===Biography===
Covenant was trained by Inquisitor [[Argento]], but along with Inquisitor [[Idris (Inquisitor)|Idris]] were forced to slay their master after he attempted to create a [[Living Saint]] to hold the [[Emperor]]'s spirit. Afterwards the duo were both named full Inquisitors of the [[Ordo Malleus]].{{Fn|3a}} He later took part in the [[Siege of Malogrim Hive]]{{Fn|4}} and is responsible for the training of Daemonhuntress [[Ivixia Dannica]].{{Fn|2}}

Recently he has begun hunting [[Radical]] Inquisitors within his order. This brought him into conflict with the heretical Inquisitor [[Goldoran Talicto]].{{Fn|3b}} However, upon being accused on [[Ero]], Talicto revealed his plans to murder the entire Inquisitorial conclave present there by overloading the Ero Reliquary Tower's Plasma Generator and assume command of the [[Caradryad Crusade]]. Revealing he also commanded a force of assassins known as [[The Renewed]], fierce fighting broke out across Reliquary Tower. Idris died preventing the [[plasma reactor]] overloading but it was revealed that "Talicto" was in fact an impostor: the real Inquisitor had died years ago and had been replaced by an agent of [[The Triumvirate]].{{Fn|3c}} Teaming up with Inquisitor [[Vult]], Covenant chased The Triumvirate to a hidden asteroid base but were assailed by unleashed [[Daemon]]s. Thanks to the sacrifice of Vult, Covenant and his retinue were able to escape The Archive before it was destroyed by the traitor [[frigate]] ''[[Truth Eternal]]''.{{Fn|3d}}

Continuing his investigation against The Triumvirate, Covenant used an [[Imperial Tarot]] deck given to him by his former [[Argento]]. In a psychic ritual, he learned that the Triumvirate was seeking a vessel for divine incarnation dubbed the "prospect". The ritual pointed him towards a monastery on [[Dominicus Prime]]. More disturbingly, Covenant learned that he is "missing" from the future.{{Fn|5a}} Arriving at Dominicus Prime via the vessel ''[[Dionysia]]'', he confronted [[Bishop]] [[Xilita]] and declared himself a judge in the Emperor's name. Covenant discovered that chaos was erupting across Dominicus and sought to organize [[Arbites]] forces in its defence.{{Fn|5b}}

Leading the Arbites against [[Mutant]] hordes dubbed the [[Red Pilgrims]], Covenant was able to finally track down and battle two members of the Covenant: [[Memnon the Wanderer]] and [[Cinis]]. During the battle the "Prospect" was able to manifest through the [[Drill Abbot]] [[Iacto]], who was transformed into a corrupted effigy. This caused the entire monastery to collapse in volcanic upheavals as Covenant was overcome by its power and fell to his knees weeping.{{Fn|5c}}{{Fn|5d}}

===Retinue===
*[[Cleander von Castellan]] - [[Rogue Trader]] pledged to serve Covenant in exchange for not being punished for dealing with [[xenos]]. Commands the vessel ''[[Dionysia]]''.{{Fn|1b}}
*[[Viola von Castellan]] - Cleander's sister who acts as a logistical specialist.{{Fn|3e}}

*[[Glavius-4-Rho]] - [[Magos]] in charge of maintaining [[Ero]]'s Reliquary Tower's reactor. After the towers destruction by the heretical Inquisitor [[Goldoran Talicto]] he has joined Covenant's retinue.{{Fn|3f}}

Valroth's truce with the Imperium also ended shortly after.{{Fn|1}} The Imperial forces, too depleted to continue their mission against the Tau, were allowed to withdraw from Tau Space and were given honours for their assistance.{{Fn|2}}

Ctesias.wikitext:
{{ThousandSonsPortal}}
'''Ctesias''' is a member of the [[Thousand Sons]] who was exiled by [[Magnus the Red]] for participating in the [[Rubric of Ahriman]]. He was a talented sorcerer who specialized in daemonology, particularly the controlling and subjugating daemons to his will. Being able to summon countless creatures from the Warp, he is a key element in [[Ahriman]]'s plan to attack the [[Planet of Sorcerers]] to enact the Second Rubric.{{Fn|1a}}

==History==
While other sorcerers often controlled daemons by binding their names into hardcopy forms, such as grimoires, Ctesias is able to control daemons with mnemonic exercises. After learning their true names and committing them to memory, he "splits" such names into discreet segments that remain apart until he wishes to summons that daemon, effectively "forgetting" a true name he has learned until he wishes to recall it. Nevertheless, this activity seems to impact on his body and in fact he appears much more frail and old than other legionaries.{{Fn|1a}}

It's later revealed that he's struck an agreement with [[Be'lakor]] in order to be protected after his death from the vengeful daemons he controls. After Ctesias's first death at the hands of a [[Flesh Hound]] Be'lakor comes to claim Ctesias. Ahriman intervenes, trying to negotiate for Ctesias's life. Be'lakor tried to induce Ahriman to his service against the whole Chaos Pantheon, and eventually ceding that his deal with Ctesias was part of a long-term plan to meet with Ahriman in person. Despite the daemon's plans, Ahriman had managed to outmaneuver the Daemon Prince and coerce him into a pact that would resurrect Ctesias and free the summoner of his own obligations.{{Fn|2}}

Ctesias would continue service in the Prodigal Sons, and would eventually play a pivotal role in the battle that concluded in the second Rubric. His army of daemons being a much needed boon for the Prodigal Sons, and especially having subjugated [[Doombreed]] to counter a Thousand Son Titan would prove to be the most deciding factor in the battle.{{Fn|1b}}

{{PAGENAME}} accompanies Ahriman and the rest of his inner circle in a bid to reverse the effects of the devastating [[Pyrodomon]].{{Fn|3a}} As Ahriman accesses the [[Necron]] time-manipulating device known as the [[Key of Infinity]], Ctesias and [[Ignis]] are able to discover that the source of the Pyrodomon to be [[ Helio Isidorus]]. Ctesias enters Isidorus' mind, destroying key memories to contain the Pyrodomon's spread at the cost of the Sorcerer's own life.{{Fn|3b}} In the past, Ahriman is able to work with Ctesias and the rest of his Cabal once more, battling the resurgent Pyrdomon and [[Setekh (Phaeron)|Setekh]].{{Fn|4a}} Ahriman is seemingly killed by a group of [[Daemon]]s dubbed the [[Bitter Kin]], but Ctesias is able to enter his mind and communicate with the Sorcerer.{{Fn|4b}} Ahriman hatches a plan to have Ctesias erase his mind once more, adopting the name "Horkos" to hide from the Pyrodomon and reach the Key of Infinity. Ctesias agrees at the cost of his own life just as Setekh and his [[Flayed One]]s attack their flagship ''[[Hekaton]]''.{{Fn|4c}} Ahriman is able to use the Key to create a new timeline where the Pyrodomon does not exist, and Ctesias is seen alongside Ahriman's side once more.{{Fn|4d}}

Ctesias would later die at an undetermined point in the future from unknown causes. His last actions would be putting to paper his recollection of the fateful encounter between Ahriman and Be'lakor that spared him from his first death.{{Fn|2}}

==Trivia==
{{Trivia}}
[[wikipedia:Ctesias|Ctesias]] was the name of a Greek physician and historian from the town of Cnidus in Caria, a location in Western Anatolia and part of the [[wikipedia:Achaemenid Empire|Achaemenid Empire]]. He is likely the inspiration for Ctesias in Warhammer 40k.

{{EmperorsChildrenPortal}}
{{Spoiler|source=The Damnation of Pythos (Novel)}}
'''Ancient {{PAGENAME}}''' was a [[Space Marine Dreadnought|Dreadnought]] of the [[Emperor's Children]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]], active during the [[Great Crusade]] and was known as a philosopher of the [[Imperium]]'s war to claim the stars. 

When the [[Horus Heresy]] began however, Curval joined his [[Primarch]] [[Fulgrim]] in turning upon the [[Emperor]] and began preaching about the perversions of the flesh and encouraged his Legion to commit debase acts, in order to increase their sensations. In the aftermath of the [[Dropsite Massacre]], Curval was among [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] [[Kleos]]' forces aboard the [[Battle Barge]] ''[[Callidora]]''{{Fn|1a}}, which was part of a large Emperor's Children fleet. However, the fleet's [[Lord Commander]] later ordered Kleos to take the Callidora to the [[Hamartia System]], along with the [[Escorts]] ''[[Infinite Sublime]]'' and the ''[[Golden Mean]]'', in order to continue to strike against the Imperium. When they arrived though, they were ambushed by the [[Iron Hands]] [[Strike Cruiser]] ''[[Veritas Ferrum]]'', which was commanded by the vengeful Captain [[Durun Atticus]], who was eager to strike a blow against the [[Traitor]]s. Having been forewarned in advance of the ''Callidora's'' arrival by his [[Astropath]] [[Rhydia Erephren]], Atticus had his crew lay space mines where the Emperor's Children's ships would enter the system; this led to the destruction of the ''Infinite Sublime'' and crippled the ''Golden Mean''. When the mines exploded, the ''Veritas Ferrum'' struck and finished off the ''Golden Mean'', before attacking the wounded ''Callidora'' and then launching [[boarding torpedoes]] at the Battle Barge.{{Fn|1b}} Curval came to the Battle Barge's defence and clashed with the invading forces led by [[Space Marine Sergeant|Sergeant]] [[Anton Galba]], where he proved to be more than a match for the Iron Hands. This ended though, when Galba ordered his forces to use [[melta charge]]s that sent the Dreadnought toppling to the floor beneath them. Curval survived the fall, but played no further part in defending the ''Callidora'' and before the Iron Hands escaped, they were able to send the Battle Barge into an [[asteroid field]], where it was destroyed.{{Fn|1a}}

Cyrius.wikitext:
{{EmperorsChildrenPortal}}
[[Lord Commander]] '''Cyrius''' was a [[Space Marine Commander]] of the [[Emperor's Children]]. He was the second to kill [[Lucius the Eternal]], and was later damned to being trapped within his victim's armour for all eternity.

==History==
Cyrius was [[Chemos]]ian by birth, inducted into the Emperor's Children Legion after [[Fulgrim]]'s rediscovery. He quickly earned a reputation as an excellent swordsman and intelligent warrior, thus rising in the [[Primarch]]'s favor. Notably, Cyrius was among the seven Legionaries that accompanied Fulgrim during the [[compliance]] of [[Byzas]].{{Fn|4}}

Not much is known about Cyrius during the [[Horus Heresy]], but it can be assumed that he turned traitor with his legion. He was known as the "Infamous Lord Commander Cyrius".{{Fn|1}}{{Fn|2}} He fought in the [[Siege of Terra]], during which he was separated from his sworn protector [[Egil Galerius]].{{Fn|3a}}

===Death===
At some point during the [[Great Scouring]],{{Fn|3b}} Cyrius took part in the legion's gladitoral games and killed Lucius, something thought impossible due to Lucius's inhuman skill and seeming unstoppable combat style. He did manage to defeat the depraved individual, but his victory was short-lived. The [[Slaanesh|Prince of Pleasure]], not willing to let such a promising protege die, turned Cyrius slowly and painfully into Lucius over a matter of weeks: "His hair fell out in clumps, and dark lines appeared under his flesh, slowly pushing through his skin as a maze of scar tissue. Soon Lucius had emerged completely, and all that remained of his executioner was a screaming, writhing face, subsumed for eternity into Lucius's armor".{{Fn|1}}{{Fn|2}}
