Daenor.wikitext:
{{BloodAngelsPortal}}
'''Daenor''' is a [[Chaplain]] of the [[Blood Angels]] [[Death Company]].{{fn|1c}}

==Overview==
[[Image:Daenor.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Death Company Chaplain Daenor{{fn|1c}}]]
From the bloody slaughter in the [[Akatrian Heights]], to the hellish invasion of the [[Nightmare Well]], Chaplain Daenor has battled his way through some of the most horrific battles in the Blood Angels’ history. Never once has his composure failed him. Never once has he succumbed to [[Red Thirst|the Flaw]], and this alone is enough to have seen him elevated to the rank of Death Company Chaplain. No matter how dire the circumstances or dread the foe, Daenor’s icy composure never cracks. Moreover, his deep spirituality and natural leadership qualities do much to steady the warriors around him. He is a light in the darkness, a beacon of hope and fortitude amongst the smoke-wreathed hell of the battlefield, and even the most lost of his brothers follow his lead without question. Daenor is far more than a figurehead, of course. His skill in close combat is prodigious; even wielding his bulky [[crozius arcanum]] in battle, Daenor strikes and parries as quickly as any expert swordsman. It is here, in the heat of battle, that the coldly composed Chaplain reveals his true zeal. Every strike is driven with the furious strength of utter conviction. Each thunderous blow that connects hurls another broken foe to the ground, their life smote from them in the name of the Angel and the [[Emperor]].{{Fn|1a}}

During the [[Diamor Campaign]], Daenor led the [[Death Company]] in battle.{{Fn|1a}} During the battle on the planet of [[Amethal]] he clashed with [[Kharn the Betrayer]] who severed his arm and nearly killed him but was distracted by Kharn's own [[Berzerker]] - [[Korbadash]], giving Daenor the chance to escape. However all of the Death Company warriors of Daenor were killed in this battle with Kharn and his allies.{{Fn|2}} Later wounded but still ardent Daenor led the last remains of arrived Death Company warriors to the battle for the '''Pit''' '''(aka Daemonic Cage)''' at the last phase of battle on Amethal.{{Fn|1b}}

He survived that battle and continues to serve his Chapter, following the aftermath of the [[Devastation of Baal]].{{Fn|3}}

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was a Transcriber for the early [[Administratum]] during the [[Great Crusade]].{{Fn|1a}}

===History===
Dalia was born in medicae block IF-55 of the Ural Collective. She was the only child of Tethis and Moraia Cythera, both of whom were subsequently deceased. At age 3 she learned to read and write, at age 6 she was indentured to the Imperial Scriptorium, and at age 9 she was trained in the art of transcription. At age 12 she was apprenticed to Magos Ludd, and at age 15 assigned to the Hall of Transcription. Her other records included 6 commendations for accuracy, 12 citations for inciting behaviour deemed to be incompatible with working practices, and one instance of imprisonment for violating the Laws of Divine Complexity.{{Fn|1c}}

She oversaw the menial task of transcribing [[Terra]]'s accumulated knowledge to other data sources. However, after being accused by [[Tech-Priest]] [[Lukas Chrom]] of [[heresy]] against the [[Omnissiah]] for her progressive thoughts on technology, Dalia was nearly arrested and executed, but was saved by [[Koriel Zeth]], who dispatched the [[Protector]] [[Rho-Mu 31]] to bring her to [[Magma City]] on [[Mars]].{{Fn|1b}}

At age 17 Dalia was subsequently recruited by Zeth to help build the [[Akashic Reader]].{{Fn|1c}} During testing on the reactor, the [[scrapcode]] infestation released in the opening salvoes of the [[Schism of Mars]], combined with the energy of the [[Astronomican]], caused a catastrophic accident and Dalia was imbued with some of the memories of the [[Dragon of Mars]].{{Fn|1d}} Learning of this power, Zeth let Dalia, Rho-Mu 31, and others lead an expedition into the [[Noctis Labyrinth]].{{Fn|1e}} However, they were pursued by the [[Kaban Machine]], and Dalia was thought killed.{{Fn|1f}}

Later, Dalia and her surviving company instead managed to enter the holding cell of the Dragon of Mars, where she was imbued with the truth of the creature and of the Omnissiah's very nature by the [[Guardian of the Dragon]], [[Semyon]]. Semyon appointed Dalia the new Guardian of the Dragon, with Rho-Mu 31 as her protector.{{Fn|1g}} The two would keep vigil over the Labyrinth for potentially thousands of years.{{Fn|1h}}

Dalin Criid.wikitext:
{{TanithPortal}}
'''Dalin Criid''' was an [[Imperial Guard]] trooper in the [[Tanith 1st]].

==History==
{{Spoiler|source=Gaunt's Ghosts (Novel Series)}}
Dalin was born '''Dalin Kolea''', a citizen of [[Vervunhive]] on [[Verghast]] to parents [[Livy Kolea|Livy]] and [[Gol Kolea]]. Dalin was ten years old at the time of the [[Zoican]] invasion in which his mother Livy was killed.{{Fn|1a}} [[Tona Criid]], a Vervunhive [[Ganger|gang-girl]], took Dalin and his younger sister [[Yoncy Kolea|Yoncy]] under her wing and protected them during the [[Siege of Vervunhive|Vervunhive siege]].{{Fn|1b}} The trio lived rough in the ruins of the hive as the siege dragged on, stealing supplies from Imperial Guard regiments to survive. Dalin's small size made him able to steal from the [[Tanith 1st]] without being caught until the thefts were noticed by [[Trooper]] [[Dermon Caffran]] who discovered the trio and, overcoming their initial mistrust, started helping Tona keep the children safe.{{Fn|1c}}

After the defeat of [[Heritor Asphodel]] and the end of the siege Tona signed up to join the Tanith 1st as a Guardsman, and she and Caffran found Dalin and Yoncy a place amongst the hordes of regimental hangers-on. They grew up following the regiment from world to world with Tona and Caffran as their adoptive parents. Unbeknownst to either of them their biological father, Gol Kolea, survived the siege of Vervunhive and after leading a scrap-company in its defence signed up as a Sergeant of the Tanith 1st. Gol was conflicted over whether or not to reveal his survival to his children but decided against it, knowing that Caffran and Tona were good foster-parents and not wanting to cause any emotional confusion in his children's lives. He was eventually talked around into meeting them but received a bad head-wound on [[Phantine (planet)|Phantine]] which destroyed his memory and personality before he could.

When Dalin came of age at 18 he decided to join the Tanith 1st as a Guardsman. By this point he was aware that Gol Kolea was alive, Kolea having apparently told him so after his miraculous recovery at the hands of [[Saint Sabbat]], but still considered Caffran his father. Dalin underwent training in a RIP squad (Retraining, Indoctrination, Punishment) where he was victimized by its Sergeant, Kexie. There he befriended [[Rhen Merrt]] who was in the squad as punishment for getting into gambling debt. Merrt stuck up for Dalin when Kexie punished him unfairly for doing well in a marksmanship drill. Dalin saw his first action on the Chaos-held world of [[Gereon]] during its liberation, where to his crushing disappointment he and the rest of the RIP detail where assigned as battlefield regulars instead of joining/rejoining their prospective regiments. Dalin fought bravely in the battle he was thrown into, showing great courage and initiative despite the overwhelming senselessness and brutality of the situation. During the fight he and Merrt saved each other's lives more than once and both came through alive, though Dalin was forever scarred by his initiation into war. Dalin and Merrt joined/rejoined the Tanith 1st after the liberation, where Dalin was stunned to discover his foster-father Caffran had been tragically killed by a frightened civilian child.

Dalin's first campaign as a Tanith trooper occurred on [[Jago]] where he was placed in [[Flyn Meryn]]'s E company to take the spot left vacant by Caffran. He was frustrated by the special treatment he received as the foster-son of two famous Sergeants, wishing to be treated just like the rest of the troopers. After Captain Meryn's adjutant Fargher was killed by [[Blood Pact]] troopers Meryn made Dalin his adjutant, partly because of his parents but also because of his initiative and skill with maps. Encountering Gol Kolea on Jago Dalin seemed unaware that Kolea was his father in what is likely a continuity error by [[Gaunt's Ghosts (Novel Series)]] author Dan Abnett.

Towards the end of the siege of the Hinzerhaus by Blood Pact forces E company was tasked with defending L company as they secured vital munitions being airlifted in. After the destruction of the transport E company took heavy losses defending a secondary gate into the Hinzerhaus. Dalin and Captain Meryn were among the few survivors, heroically fighting off the Blood Pact until they were relieved by [[Ban Daur]]'s G company.

During the final assault on [[Urdesh]] against the [[Sons of Sek]], it is revealed that Dalian Criid had been converted into a [[Woe Machine]]. After killing his father [[Gol Kolea]], the machine was destroyed by Gaunt and the Tanith First and Only.{{Fn|2}}

Daman.wikitext:
{{BloodAngelsPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is a [[Blood Angels]] [[Space Marine Dreadnought|Dreadnought]] that serves in the [[Chapter|Chapter's]] [[6th Company (Blood Angels)|Sixth Company]].  He defended their [[Fortress Monastery]] on [[Baal]], when it was [[Devastation of Baal|invaded]] by [[Hive Fleet Leviathan]] and was among the Chapter's forces that rushed to protect the '''Hall of Sarcophagi''' when it came under attack.  However, due to their slow speed, {{PAGENAME}} and two of his Dreadnought [[Battle Brother]]s were left behind by the other responding forces.  When they finally reached the Hall of Sarcophagi, the Blood Angels protecting it were being overwhelmed by hordes of [[Genestealer]]s and the Dreadnoughts ended the battle by opening fire on the [[Xenos]].  In the aftermath of the attack, though, nearly all the Sarcophagi containing the Chapter's sleeping [[Aspirant]]s were destroyed and most of the Blood Angels who had tried to protect them were dead.  This included the Dreadnoughts' [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]], [[Raxiatel]], and {{PAGENAME}} lamented that they had not been able to arrive in time to save their Battle Brothers.  Afterwards, {{PAGENAME}} continued to take part in the battle against the [[Tyranid]]s{{Fn|1a}}, but it is not known if he survived to see Hive Fleet Leviathan defeated.{{Fn|1b}}

Damien Bloodhound.wikitext:
{{InquisitionPortal}}
[[Image:Damian.jpg|thumb|right|120px|Damien Bloodhound{{Fn|2}}]]
'''Damien Bloodhound''' is a rogue and outlaw [[Necromunda (planet)|Necromunda]] [[Adeptus Arbites]] [[Enforcer (Inquisition)|Enforcer]], who now works as a bodyguard and [[Bounty Hunter]].{{Fn|1}}
==History==
He is the son of a [[96th Connacht Rangers]] [[Colonel]] and became a [[Necromunda (planet)|Necromunda]] [[Adeptus Arbites]] [[Enforcer (Inquisition)|Enforcer]], after his induction into a [[Schola Progenium]]. In his career on the [[Hive World]], Damien had an uncanny ability, almost seemingly preternatural, in predicting the behavioral patterns of criminals. This was an asset that made him into an excellent hunter, but Damien's brutal methods earned hm a fearsome reputation. However in order to maintain this, he developed a tough physical and mental regime, which eventually made Damien an addict to the illegal [[Narcotic]] [[Crash]]. In time, his dependency led him to form a pact with the [[Underhive]] [[gang]] lord [[Jerzek Fallon]], who supplied Damien with Crash and was sold bounties in return.{{Fn|1}} 

Their relationship was eventually found by Damian's superiors, who then sought to apprehend him. However the outlaw was able to escape into space aboard a smuggling spaceship, though not before executing [[Jerzek Fallon|Fallon]] with an overdose of [[Crash]]. Damien now works as a bodyguard and [[Bounty Hunter]] to the highest bidder and still uses his [[Enforcer Shotgun]], which he arms with his own developed highly illegal loads. Because of his expertise Damien also often works with [[Inquisitor]]s, but he rarely stays employed with one for long, for fear of them discovering his past.{{Fn|1}}

'''Dane''' is the [[Dark Angels Grand Master|Grand Master]] of the [[Knights of the Crimson Order]], a [[Dark Angels]] [[Successor Chapter]].{{Fn|1a}}

==Biography==
He an accomplished fleet commander,{{Fn|1b}} who is utterly loyal to the [[Dark Angels]]' [[Dark Angels Grand Master|Supreme Grand Master]] [[Azrael]]. This was mentioned to the Supreme Grand Master by [[Chief Librarian]] [[Ezekiel]], when Azrael was surprised to see the Crimson Order amongst the [[Unforgiven]] who came to aid the Dark Angels during the [[Battle of the Caliban System]]. This was despite Dane's [[Chapter]] having suffered many casualties in their latest campaigns. Ezekiel replied that the [[Dark Angels Grand Master|Grand Master]] would willingly lead the last of the Crimson Order into their enemies, to uphold Crimson Order's honour in Azrael's eyes. Because of this, the Chief Librarian told the Supreme Grand Master that there was no need to worry if Dane needed to be told the [[Cypher|truth]] of what [[Tuchulcha|caused]] the Battle of the Caliban System to occur. Ezekiel knew the Grand Master would follow Azrael's lead and not pry too deeply into the matter.{{Fn|1a}} The Supreme Grand Master agreed to this and would later give Dane command of the Dark Angels' and Unforgiven's fleet due to his skills in void warfare. Dane would do so from aboard his flagship, the [[Battle Barge]]{{Fn|1b}} ''[[Flame of Galandros]]''.{{Fn|1a}}

([[Era Indomitus]]) |Notes = }} '''Dante''' is the current [[Chapter Master]] of the [[Blood Angels]]. Commander Dante is one of the most experienced and able [[Space Marine]] commanders. In no small part, this is due to the longevity of the [[Blood Angels]], which he has ruled for 1,100 years. Dante is the oldest living Space Marine in the [[Imperium]] (excluding [[Dreadnought]]s) and is held in awe by leaders of other [[Chapter]]s, who can remember him being a famous commander when they were in the [[Scout Company]].{{Fn|1}}{{Fn|3}} ==Biography== ===Early life=== Luis Dante{{Fn|8b}} was born in 447.[[M40]]{{Fn|6a}} on [[Baal Secundus]] ([[Baal]]'s second moon) and his growth was stunted by malnutrition and radiation.{{Fn|5}} Dante was part of his planet's salt clans, a nomadic people that travelled the salt deserts (former seas) of Baal Secundus to harvest its salt, selling it at various permanent settlements at the salt deserts' borders. His mother died giving birth to his stillborn younger brother, and he was thus raised by his father [[Arreas]]. His childhood was hard, with his clan facing dangerous wildlife, human raiders, and an extremely hostile environment; most clan members died before their 30th year. From an early age, Dante felt the desire to help others and make a difference; thus, he was drawn to the idea of becoming a Blood Angel. His father, who did not want to lose his last living relative, forbid him from partaking in the [[Angel's Fall]] trials to determine the next [[Aspirant]]s. Undeterred, Dante regretfully left in secret, crossing the [[Great Salt Waste]] alone to reach the trials.{{Fn|6a}}{{Fn|6c}} He almost died of thirst, but also first experienced a vision of the [[Sanguinor]] who guided him to a mummified corpse with intact water flasks, saving his life and allowing him to continue his journey.{{Fn|6c}} When he took part in his clans trials at the Place of Challenge he showed no special promise, but nonetheless survived. Afterwards he was inducted by [[Chaplain]] [[Malafael]] into the [[Blood Angels]] Chapter as an [[Aspirant]] under [[Sanguinary Priest]] [[Araezon]]. He first drew notice when during his transformation after drinking the [[gene-seed]] synthesized blood of [[Sanguinius]], he went into a year long coma and cried out the names of fallen primarchs, dark gods, and long-banished [[Daemon]]s. Upon emerging Dante was trained to become a battle-brother, then Brother-Sergeant.{{Fn|5}} He reached the rank of [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] in 753.M40.{{Fn|6b}} Later he took part in the [[Kallius Insurrection]] of [[M40]], where every Captain of the Blood Angels but Dante himself was slain, and it was decided by the gathered [[Chaplain]]s and [[Sanguinary Priest]]s that he would become the new [[Chapter Master]].{{Fn|5}} ===Chapter Master=== His very presence inspires troops to acts of valour that are extraordinary even for Space Marines. Because of this reputation, when it came to choosing a leader for the [[Armageddon]] intervention, the Masters of the other two Chapters taking part (the [[Salamanders]] and the [[Ultramarines]]) unanimously asked for him to be placed in charge.{{Fn|1}} Dante is a legend not just amongst the Blood Angels but also amongst the common citizenry of the Imperium, to whom he is a saviour, a golden-armoured hero who descends to save them in their darkest hour.{{Fn|3}} Commander Dante has led the Blood Angels to some of their greatest victories, from the bloody campaigns in [[Ultima Macharia]] to the [[Liberation of Canau]]. He clove the mighty [[Bloodthirster]] [[Skarbrand]] in two at the [[Gates of Pandemonium]] and drove the [[Ork]]s from the twelve worlds of [[Blackfang]].{{Fn|5}} Perhaps his most famous victories were in the [[Second War for Armageddon]], where his leadership allowed the beleaguered defenders to triumph over the fury of [[Waaagh! Ghazghkull]]. There he led the valiant strike against the Orks attacking [[Hive Acheron]], where the horde was ripped asunder by cannon and bomb as Dante spearheaded the reinforcements. And it was in the closing stages of the war that Dante's tactical genius finally broke the back of the Ork army, leading a massed [[Drop Pod]] assault against the Orks assaulting [[Hive Tartarus]], his Blood Angels slaying fully half of the Orks and driving them back to the ash wastes and jungles.{{Fn|3}} In the closing days of the 41st Millennium, heroes like Dante were points of light in the growing darkness. He stood, as he had done for a millennium or more, between the enemies of Mankind and the Imperium.{{Fn|3}} As a leader, Dante is utterly fearless, and full of drive and initiative. If his opponents ever make a mistake, Dante is on it in a flash, and he always exploits their error to the fullest. He has a reputation for leading from the front and can usually be found where the battle is fiercest. Plummeting from the skies at the head of his [[Sanguinary Guard|personal bodyguard]], a halo of power playing around his head.{{Fn|1}} Yet for all of his success, or perhaps because of it, Dante had grown weary of his burdens. He had lived far longer than he should, and the burden of centuries grew even weightier. Only one thing prevented Dante from succumbing to ennui- recorded in the Scrolls of [[Sanguinius]] were the [[Primarch]]s visions of a great battle to overshadow all others, where one golden warrior would stand between his [[Emperor]] and the darkness. For many generations of the Blood Angels, these prophecies had been read as Sanguinius's foreknowledge of his own fate. Yet through some instinct- perhaps a lingering trace of his Primarch's fabled far-seeing eye, or his own prophetic dreams of the golden warrior,{{Fn|8a}} Dante believed otherwise. He frequently believed that one day, the defence of the Emperor would possibly rest in his hands, and he aimed to fulfil that final duty.{{Fn|4}} [[Image:Dante by nuala kinrade.JPG|thumb|right|200px|Commander Dante{{Fn|13}}]] ====Devastation of Baal==== This belief would come to be understood finally during the [[Devastation of Baal]], when Dante led the Blood Angels and their successor chapter's in a final stand against [[Hive Fleet Leviathan]]. During the battle Dante managed to slay the [[Swarmlord]] but was badly wounded in the process. As he lay dying, he saw a vision of the Sanguinor and [[Sanguinius]] himself. Relieved that his duty was finally over, Dante was about to pass into death when Sanguinius told him to live and that his time was not yet done. Distressed, Dante begged Sanguinius to let him die and take his soul with him, but was suddenly revived on the battlefield.{{Fn|8b}} Fortunately for the Chapter Master, Baal was saved by [[Roboute Guilliman]] and the [[Indomitus Crusade]],{{Fn|7}} who commended him for saving half the galaxy from the terror of the Hive Fleet.{{Fn|8b}} Following the salvation of Baal, Guilliman named Dante the Lord Regent of [[Imperium Nihilus]].{{Fn|9}} He used his new authority to organize an offensive to retake the [[Red Scar]] region from the tendrils of Leviathan known as the [[Angel's Halo]].{{Fn|10}} He has since undergone the [[Rubicon Primaris|operation]] to become a [[Primaris Space Marine]].{{Fn|14}} ====Arks of Omen==== During the [[Arks of Omen Campaign]] Dante led a force of [[Blood Angels]] to intercept an Ark that was targeting the [[agri world]]s of the [[Saganas Belt]]. Upon arrival they found the Ark, [[Night Terror]], drifting in the voide with wrecked heretic warships around it. After boarding it they found dead heretics, astartes and humans, who had been slain by bolter rounds and a large sword, they also found sulpherous residue, the remains of biomechanical infestation mixed with something that resembled wilted plant life. After searching for several days they couldn't find any more clues as to what happened, and Dante ordered samples to be analyzed.{{Fn|19}} Dante was the first high-ranking Imperial official to discover that [[Lion El'Jonson]] had returned after ten thousand years of absence after investigating reports of his return. Dante informed the Lion of recent developments in the Galaxy and that [[Roboute Guilliman]] lived.{{Fn|17}} Taking the Lion aboard his flagship ''[[Absolution's Ire]]'', Dante and [[Imperial Navy]] reinforcements made for the [[Somnium Stars]] to rescue the [[Dark Angels]] and [[Unforgiven]] from the clutches of [[Vashtorr]].{{Fn|16a}} During the subsequent [[Battle of Idolatros]], Dante arrived to save [[Azrael]] and the Dark Angels aboard [[Wyrmwood]] just as they were about to be overrun by [[Angron]] and his [[World Eaters]]. Alongside his [[Sanguinary Guard]], [[Assault Squad]]s, and [[Redemptor Dreadnought]]s, Dante met the [[Daemon Primarch]] in battle but all were swept aside by the Daemon's fury. As the final blow was about to be struck on the injured Dante, The Lion appeared and intercepted the blow deal.{{Fn|16a}} Dante was subsequently recovered by Azrael and his warriors, and upon regaining his composure was able to coordinate the evacuation of Wyrmwood alongside the Unforgiven.{{Fn|16b}} ==Wargear== Dante's [[Artificer Armour]] incorporates a [[Jump Pack]] and the [[Death Mask of Sanguinius]], a golden mask said to have been modeled on the features of the [[Blood Angels]]' [[Primarch]] [[Sanguinius]]. A halo of golden energy plays about Dante's head striking terror into the hearts of his enemies. Dante is also armed with the [[Axe Mortalis]] and the [[Perdition Pistol]].{{Fn|2}} Since Dante [[Rubicon Primaris|became]] a [[Primaris Space Marine]], both weapons have now been upscaled to suit his newly massive frame.{{Fn|14}} ==Images== Dante2nd.jpg|Dante (2nd Edition){{Fn|11}} Dante Primaris.jpg|Dante as a [[Primaris Space Marine]]{{Fn|14}} JoytoyUltraBloodAngelsDante.jpeg|Joytoy Dante figure{{Fn|18}} PICFILE -BA6824593.jpg| Artisan's imagining of [[Dante]] witnessing the arrival of [[Roboute Guilliman]].{{Fn|20}} ===Videos=== *''Commander Dante Rises Anew'':{{Fn|15}} {{#evt: service=youtube |id=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wzWuBDlFYsM |alignment=center |description= |container=frame }} ==See also== *[[List of Chapter Masters]] *[[Dante: Lord of the Host (Short Story)]] ==Sources== {{Cite}} *{{Endn|1}}: [[Codex: Blood Angels (3rd Edition)]], {{Cite This}} *{{Endn|2}}: [[Codex: Blood Angels (4th Edition)]], pg. 6 *{{Endn|3}}: [http://www.games-workshop.com/en-US/Blood-Angels-Commander-Dante Blood Angels Character focus at Games Workshop] ''(last accessed 14 April 2015)'' *{{Endn|4}}: [[Codex: Blood Angels (5th Edition)]], pg. 53 *{{Endn|5}}: [[Warlords of the Dark Millennium: Dante (Background Book)]] {{Cite this}} *6: [[Dante (Novel)]]: **{{Endn|6a}}: Chapter One **{{Endn|6b}}: Chapter Twenty **{{Endn|6c}}: Chapter Three *{{Endn|7}}: [[Codex: Tyranids (8th Edition)]], pg. 63 *8: [[The Devastation of Baal (Novel)]]: **{{Endn|8a}}: Chapter Fifteen **{{Endn|8b}}: Chapter Twenty-Nine *{{Endn|9}}: [[Codex: Blood Angels (8th Edition)]], pg. 22 *{{Endn|10}}: [[Psychic Awakening: Blood of Baal]], pgs. 8-9 *{{Endn|11}}: [[Codex: Angels of Death (2nd Edition)]], pg. 59 *{{Endn|12}}: [http://web.archive.org/web/20140426213051/http://www.blacklibrary.com/games-workshop-digital-editions/Dante.html Black Library: Warlords of the Dark Millennium: Dante - Dark Father.wikitext:
{{DrukhariPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' is the mysterious leader of the [[Incubi]] sect of [[Dark Eldar]].{{Fn|1}}

==History==
The Dark Father is the head of the Incubi sect, and is thus the most powerful Incubus in existence, due to the manner in which seniority is decided in [[Commorragh]]. It is believed that [[Arhra]], founder of the [[Eldar]] [[Aspect]] of the [[Striking Scorpion]]s is the original Dark Father, although this cannot be confirmed. In the event that Arhra did found the Incubi sect, it likewise cannot be confirmed that he was not killed by one of his students, and thus overthrown as Dark Father.

The argument for Arhra being the founder of the Incubi is based primarily on the fact that Eldar refer to Arhra specifically as "The Fallen Phoenix", and refer to Incubi as "Fallen Warriors", stating that their Dark Father had, "Turned from the light into the shadows". This, coupled with the great similarities between the Incubi [[Tormentor Helm|Tormentor Helms]] and the [[Striking Scorpion]]'s [[Mandiblaster]]s, and the aesthetic similarity of the scorpion stylings between both warriors lead most to this conclusion, although it has never been confirmed.

==Sources==

Dathan Tychor.wikitext:
{{ImperialFistsPortal}}
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was an [[Excoriators]] [[Space Marine Sergeant]] during the [[War of the Beast]] and was later chosen to represent his Chapter during the [[Feast of Blades]] held to honour the passing of the [[Imperial Commander]] [[Koorland]]. He would reach the tournament's final round, where he fought [[Maximus Thane]], [[Chapter Master]] of the [[Fists Exemplar]]; which had won the last Feast of Blades that was held. Though it was a hard fought battle, that Tychor nearly won, he was eventually defeated by the Chapter Master, but earned himself much acclaim from those who witnessed their fight{{Fn|1a}}. Thane was left so impressed by the Sergeant's skills, shown during their fight{{Fn|1b}}, that when the [[Successor Chapter]]s decided to rebuild their destroyed [[Second Founding|Progenitor Chapter]]{{Fn|1a}}, Tychor was chosen to become one of the new Imperial Fists. He would later take part in the [[Imperium]]'s third invasion, of [[The Beast]]'s Homeworld [[Ullanor]], where Thane honoured him by making the former Sergeant, the rebuilt Imperial Fists' [[Standard Bearer]] and [[Chapter Champion]]. He was also charged with leading Thane's [[Honour Guard]]{{Fn|1b}} and during the Imperial Fists' battle with The Beast, Tychor fulfilled his duty by taking a fatal blow from the [[Warboss|Warlord]], that would have killed the Chapter Master.{{Fn|1c}}

Decario.wikitext:
{{SpaceMarinesPortal}}
'''Decario''' is the [[Chief Librarian]] of the [[Relictors]] [[chapter]] and was the first member of his Chapter to make use of [[daemon]] weapons against the forces of [[Chaos]].{{Fn|1}}{{Fn|2a}}

==History==
The Relictors, then known as the [[Fire Claws]], mobilised to intercept a badly damaged [[Space Hulk]] named the ''[[Captor of Sin]]'' as it left warp space near the [[Stygies System]].{{Fn|2a}}{{Fn|2b}}  Decario, [[Inquisitor]] [[de Marche]] and [[Terminator Assault Squad]]s entered the hulk and encountered the forces of a renegade warband led by a [[Tzeentch|Tzeentchian]] [[Chaos Champion|champion]] named [[Excoriator (Chaos Champion)|the Excoriator]].  De Marche was badly wounded by the champion and Decario's [[Force Sword]] was broken but he managed to use his [[Power Fist]] to rip the Excoriator's sword arm from its socket.  Even so, the Excoriator went on to kill another four terminators and force Decario to the ground.  Decario muttered a prayer to the [[Emperor of Mankind|Emperor]] and reached out for the nearest weapon, picking up the [[Daemon Sword]] of the Excoriator and beheading him.{{Fn|1}}{{Fn|2a}}

From that moment on Decario sensed he could use these weapons against [[Chaos]].  De Marche warned Decario to put the sword down, as he was the only one in the party who could control the powers held within the daemon sword.  Decario handed over the weapon but would never be free of the power he felt he could wield with it.  De Marche had similar feelings to Decario and together they convinced the [[Chapter Master]] of this and they embarked on a crusade to locate similar relics which they could use against Chaos, around the [[Eye of Terror]].{{Fn|1}}{{Fn|2a}}

{{NightLordsPortal}}
'''Decimus''' is the '''Prophet of the Eighth Legion''' and leader of a warband of [[Night Lords]] formerly of the 10th Company, previously led by [[Talos Valcoran]].

==Biography==
'''Decimus''' is a young [[Space Marine]] carrying the gene-seed taken from [[Talos Valcoran]] by [[Variel|Variel the Flayer]]. He may be the son of two of Talos's slaves, [[Septimus]] and the [[Navigator]] [[Octavia]], as Talos warned them Variel would come for their child one night if he survived [[Tsagualsa]].{{fn|1a}} He inherited Talos's ability of foresight, as well as his sword [[Aurum (Sword)|Aurum]] and the twin-linked boltgun of the War-Sage [[Malcharion]]. Other affectations adopted from the [[First Claw]] include the aquila on his armour being ritually broken in the same manner as Talos, a cloak of flayed skin as [[Uzas]] used to wear, and a studded helm combining the skull with the soul hunter rune of Talos, the ceremonial winged crest worn by [[Xarl]], and the lightning bolt tears of [[Cyrion]].{{fn|1b}}

At a gathering of the Legion shortly before the [[13th Black Crusade]], he prophesied that [[Ezekyle Abaddon|Abaddon]] would defeat the [[Imperium]], although a great many of the warband leaders present would die - including [[Zar Tavik]], [[Kalex]], [[Darjyr]], and [[Toriel]] the White-Handed.{{fn|1b}}

Decius XXIII.wikitext:
{{EcclesiarchyPortal}}

'''Decius XXIII''' is [[Ecclesiarch]] of the [[Adeptus Ministorum]] as of 945.[[M41]].{{Fn|1}}

==History==
Decius XXIII famously clashed with [[Inquisitor Lord]] [[Fyodor Karamazov]] of the [[Inquisition]]'s [[Ordo Hereticus]] in 945.M41 over the fate of the lowly [[Preacher]] [[Icarael]].  The confrontation almost came to outright battle after the Inquisitor executed the boy, but Decius vindicated Karamazov after taints of [[Chaos]] were found amongst the followers of Icarael.{{Fn|1}}

Later in the [[Age of the Dark Imperium]] Decius XXIII attempted  to use the instability caused by the [[Great Rift]]'s creation to repeal the [[Decree Passive]]. This caused a number of assassination attempts on him, which forced [[Saint Celestine]], [[Inquisitor]] [[Greyfax]], and [[Longinus]] to escort him to [[Ophelia VII]] for safety. However it soon became apparent the series was events was orchestrated by the [[Lord of Change]] known as the [[Tyrant of Blueflame]], causing Celestine to later execute Decius.{{Fn|2}}

==Canon Conflicts==
The later period of Decius' reign as Ecclesiarch seems to overlap with that of [[Baldo Slyst]]. In [[Our Martyred Lady (Audio Drama)]] he was still ruling when Guilliman first appeared while [[Watchers of the Throne: The Emperor's Legion (Novel)]] depicts Slyst as ruling in the same period.

Defay.wikitext:
{{OrdoHereticusPortal}}{{ChaosPortal}}
[[Image:Inquisitor Defay.jpg|thumb|280px|right|Inquisitor Defay{{Fn|2}}]]
'''Defay''' was a [[Psyker]] [[Ordo Hereticus]] [[Inquisitor Lord]], who attended the [[Thracian Primaris|Triumph of Thracian]] and fell to [[Heresy]] after investigating the [[Chaos]] taint on [[Nicodemus]]. There Defay and his [[acolyte]] [[Gravier]] discovered that the corruption lay within the noble bloodline of '''House Matheldas'''. With the aid of Nicodemus' [[Cardinal]] [[Sarthos]], they succeeded in destroying the tainted House, but it was soon revealed that the Cardinal himself, was part of the corrupt Matheldas bloodline. This led Defay and Gravier to kill the now revealed [[Heretic]] Cardinal, but Sarthos' death unleashed the [[Daemon]] that had long ago possessed him. Defay was forced to destroy the Daemon using his psychic powers, but the Inquisitor feared that in doing so, he had been corrupted by Chaos' taint. This caused Defay to immediately flee, leaving Interrogator Gravier behind and then cut off contact with the [[Inquisition]]{{Fn|1a}}. When Gravier began to search for his master, the Inquisition intervened and assigned him, as an [[Interrogator]] to Inquisitor [[Reiker]], who had been charged with finding Defay. Their search led them to [[Sepulchris]], where they confronted Defay as he was investigating how to open a [[Warp]] gate on the world. Ultimately though, Gravier's loyalty to his former master won out and Reiker was killed in the battle that followed. But by then, Defay had fallen to Heresy and he then killed Gravier, before opening the Warp portal{{Fn|1b}}. What became of Defay after this though, is not known.{{Fn|1a}}

Dellasarius.wikitext:
{{ImperiumPortal}}
{{Spoiler|source=Tallarn: Ironclad (Novel)}}''
'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was the [[Governor-Militant]] of [[Tallarn]] when the [[Iron Warriors]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]] [[Battle of Tallarn|invaded]] during the [[Horus Heresy]] and had previously served for most of his life with the [[Imperial Army]] during the [[Great Crusade]].{{Fn|1}}

When the [[Primarch]] [[Perturabo]] ordered for [[Virus Bomb]]s to be unleashed upon Tallarn, {{PAGENAME}} was able to reach one of its underground shelters and from there began to rally the world's survivors to fight the Iron Warriors; as they began to land their forces on its devastated surface. By the time other [[Loyalist]] forces from the [[Imperium]] began to arrive during the invasion, it was with {{PAGENAME}} that they met with, as he had become the leader of what remained of Tallarn's armed forces. Through sheer force of will he united the various factions and military leaders taking part in the battle and began to force them to organize and work together as they fought the Iron Warriors. It was this fact however, that nearly caused the Iron Warriors to be victorious in their invasion, as Dellasarius was later assassinated when his [[Baneblade]] was destroyed by one of the [[Vanquisher]]s commanded by his company of guards; as he journeyed in an armed convoy to another Loyalist base known as the '''Crescent Shelter'''. The reason why one of Dellasarius's loyal guards, would kill the Governor-Militant is unknown; but with the presence of the [[Alpha Legion]] on Tallarn, it is possible the [[Traitor Legion]] may have had a hand in it{{Fn|1a}}. Regardless of the reason, the death of Dellasarius sent discord throughout the Loyalist forces, as they no longer had his powerful presence to unite them, and they began to fight amongst themselves, as to how to continue the war against the Iron Warriors.{{Fn|1b}}

'''Delvarus''' was a [[Centurion (Rank)|Centurion]] of the [[World Eaters]] during the [[Great Crusade]] and [[Horus Heresy]]. He later became Warchief of [[the Riven]] and joined the [[Black Legion]].

===Biography===
'''Delvarus''' was born on [[Novus Principa]],{{fn|2d}} a [[Jungle World]] conquered by the [[World Eaters]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]] in the earliest decades of the [[Great Crusade]].{{fn|1f}} He gained a reputation for being undefeatable in the Legion's fighting pits{{fn|1a}} and when paired with [[Sigismund]] of the [[Imperial Fists]], the two won every fight to first blood in less than half a minute.{{fn|1d}} During the [[Ghenna Massacre]] most of Delvarus' squad was wiped out, including his Captain [[Barca]]. Delvarus, though a mere sergeant, was able to hold his own against the hordes of enemies.{{Fn|4}}

Delvarus commanded the 44th Company ''[[Triarii]]'', the 500 ship-to-ship boarding specialists of the Legion charged with protecting the ''[[Conqueror (Ship)|Conqueror]]''. Despite this duty, he often participated in planetary assaults.{{fn|1b}} After an unsanctioned planetary drop that left the ''Conqueror'' exposed to boarding by the [[Ultramarines]] above [[Armatura]],{{fn|1c}} Delvarus was shot by Captain [[Lotara Sarrin]] and confined to his quarters.{{fn|1e}} When he was released, he was forced to fight twenty-six third blood duels, contrary to the normal limit of eight pit fights, before being humiliated when [[Kargos]] spared his life in a ''sanguis extremis'' duel.{{fn|1f}}

By the end of the Heresy, Delvarus had become [[possessed (Chaos Space Marines)|possessed]].{{fn|3}}

Delvarus went on to lead [[the Riven]],{{fn|2d}} a brutal [[warband]] of [[Possessed (Chaos Space Marines)|Secondborn]]. He and the Riven joined the [[Black Legion]]{{fn|2a}} and became the guardians of the ''[[Vengeful Spirit]]''.{{fn|2b}} He was killed in the [[First Battle of Cadia]] by [[Thagus Daravek]] during a boarding action on the ''Vengeful Spirit''.{{fn|2c}}

===Appearance and Wargear===
Delvarus had dark skin and long, black hair - one of the few World Eaters who did not shave his head, despite the discomfort when wearing a helm. He had iron teeth and wielded a [[Meteor Hammer]].{{fn|1f}}

After possession, he was blinded by black cataracts, though his other senses were enhanced,{{fn|2b}} and his warshape had wings and a crown of horns.{{fn|2c}}

[[file:Deserter.jpg|thumb|right|220px|{{PAGENAME}}]]
The '''Deserter''' is the name given to a crazed old [[Necromunda (planet)|Necromunda]]n [[Bounty Hunter]] who lives in a booby-trapped warren within the [[underhive]] of [[Hive Primus]].

Nothing is known about the Deserter, save that by his tattoos the bounty hunter once served in the legendary [[Necromundan 8th]] [[Regiment]]. Because of this, various rumours abound about who he truly is. Some say he was a disgraced [[general]] who lost his entire regiment in some off-world war and was given the choice of execution or exile to the underhive. Others reckon he was a war hero who was grievously wounded (as his skull plate seems to attest) and then wandered down from the spire after losing his memory. Then there are those who say he is called the Deserter because that is just what he is, and [[Helmawr]]'s cronies simply stopped trying to bring him in after their enforcers kept failing to come back. Whatever the truth is, the underhive's gangs are unsure why the Deserter is tolerated by Hive Primus's authorities. This has not stopped the gangs from hiring the deserter's services, though they often need to send at least a few [[juves]] when contracting the bounty hunter, as he can be a little trigger happy when it comes to those who knock on his door. The skills he brings to a fight, however, are always worth it, as there are few individuals as talented as the Deserter when it comes to laying traps or setting ambushes.{{Fn|1}}

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was the [[Terran]] [[Chapter Master]] of the [[Word Bearers]] [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]]'s [[Serrated Sun]] [[Chapter]], during the [[Great Crusade]]{{Fn|1a}}.

After the [[Emperor]] ordered the [[Ultramarines]] Legion to destroy [[Monarchia]], the Word Bearers' [[Primarch]] [[Lorgar]] joined the Serrated Sun and told them they were going to undertake [[The Pilgrimage]].{{Fn|1b}} Their journey led them to the world [[Cadia]], near the [[Eye of Terror]], where Lorgar met with the [[Cultist]] leader [[Ingethel]]. Weeks later Deumos was among a group of Word Bearers, that accompanied Lorgar to a cave, where Ingethel had been conducting a [[Chaos]] ritual that would aid Lorgar in his Pilgrimage. However, the [[Adeptus Custodes]] [[Vendatha]], who was among a group of Custodes charged with watching the Word Bearers Legion, interrupted the horrific ritual in disgust{{Fn|1c}} and judged Lorgar a Traitor for refusing to stop it himself. Vendatha then tried to contact the other Custodes in the Word Bearers fleet in orbit, but was told by Lorgar that the cave was blocking his signal. Feeling that he had no choice after witnessing such heresy, Vendatha launched an attack to kill Lorgar, but Deumos, [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] [[Tsar Quorel]] and his Company [[Chaplain]] [[Rikus]], stood in front of the Custode to defend their [[Primarch]]. However, they were no match for the skilled Vendatha, who easily killed all of them in seconds.{{Fn|1d}}

(Formerly) **[[Sons of Horus]] **[[13th Company (Sons of Horus)|13th Company]] *[[Black Legion]] **[[Chosen of Abaddon]] **[[Children of Torment]] *[[Slaanesh]] |Notes = }} '''Devram Korda''', also known as the '''Tyrant of Sarora''', is a [[Chaos Lord]] of the [[Black Legion]] and one of the [[Chosen of Abaddon]].{{Fn|1}} A follower of [[Slaanesh]], he is one of the commanders of the Black Legion's [[Children of Torment]].{{Fn|4}} ===Biography=== ====Horus Heresy==== During the early stages of the [[Horus Heresy]], Korda was a [[Space Marine Veteran Sergeant|Veteran Sergeant]] in the [[Sons of Horus]] [[13th Company (Sons of Horus)|13th Company]]. A common companion of his [[Space Marine Company|Company]] [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]], [[Luc Sedirae]], Korda was present when Sedirae and [[Erebus]] of the [[Word Bearers]] unmasked a [[Clade Veneum]] assassination attempt on the [[Warmaster]] [[Horus]], and in fact slew the [[assassin]], [[Tobeld]], himself.{{Fn|3a}} Some time later, the 13th Company were part of Horus' forces when the warmaster determined to visit the world of [[Dagonet]]. For reasons currently unclear, Horus decided to use a proxy for this visit, and Luc Sedirae was selected for this honour. Arriving on the planet dressed in the warmaster's [[Terminator armour|plate and mantle]], Sedirae was almost immediately the victim of a assassination. That the assassination was meant to kill Horus only increased the ire of Korda and the rest of 13th Company, who were loosed onto the world to exact bloody vengeance for the death of their Captain. A sorrowful Devram Korda commanded this retributive campaign.{{Fn|3b}} ====The Tyrant of Sarora==== As a Chaos Lord, Korda became known for his heinous actions on [[Sarora]]. There, he distilled the life essence of the citizens of the planet's largest [[hive]] for a single vial of elixir, which made him virtually invincible. Following that, he conquered the entire system and ruled it with an iron fist, distilling more elixirs from the hives under his dominion until he was toppled by rival Chaos Space Marines from the [[Emperor's Children]].{{Fn|1}} ====The Heart of Chaos==== At the beginning of his [[13th Black Crusade]], [[Abaddon]] sent Korda and his fellow Chosen on a quest to find and retrieve the mystical "[[Heart of Chaos]]", an artefact said to exist at the very centre of the [[Eye of Terror]]. Somehow [[Imperium|Imperial]] agents found out about this mission and sent an [[Officio Assassinorum Execution Force|Execution Force]] after the Chosen of Abaddon. Korda himself was initially declared the primary target.{{Fn|1}} Despite this, he overcame all hurdles on his journey and successfully returned in the latter days of the war. Together with his peer, the [[sorcerer]] [[Ygethmor]], Korda handed the Heart of Chaos over to his master, bringing Abaddon's plans for it closer to fruition.{{Fn|2}} ===See also=== *[[List of Chaos Lords]] ===Sources=== *{{Endn|1}}: [[Codex: Chaos Space Marines (3rd Edition, 2nd Codex)]], pg. 10 *{{Endn|2}}: [[White Dwarf 287 (UK)]], pg. 36 - ''Death by a Thousand Cuts'' *3: [[Nemesis (Novel)]]: **{{Endn|3a}}: Chapter One **{{Endn|3b}}: Chapter Fifteen *{{Endn|4}}: [[Codex: Chaos Space Marines (8th Edition)]], pg. 19 — ''Black Legion Warbands'' *{{Endn|5}}: [[Battlefleet Gothic: Armada II]] {{DEFAULTSORT:Korda, Devram}} [[Category:Characters (Black Crusades)]] [[Category:Characters (Black Legion)]] [[Category:Characters (Horus Heresy)]] [[Category:Characters (Slaanesh)]] [[Category:Characters (Sons of Horus)]] [[de:Devram Korda]]

'''{{PAGENAME}}''' was a [[Tribune (Adeptus Custodes)|Tribune]]{{Fn|1}} and [[Shield-Captain|Prefect]] of the [[Hykanatoi]] caste of the [[Custodian Guard]] during the [[Great Crusade]] and [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|1}}

===History===
Diocletian was amongst the earliest members of the Custodes and had served in the [[Hetaeron Guard]].{{Fn|8}} Falling under the command of Tribune [[Ra Endymion]], during the [[War Within the Webway]] Diocletian was charged with organizing a fresh wave of Imperial forces to resist the [[Chaos]] forces in the [[Webway]] including the condemned prisoners of [[House Vyridion]]. During the final battle for the portal Diocletian fought alongside both Ra and the [[Emperor]] himself, eventually managing to evacuate the Webway and make it back to [[Terra]]. After the battle the Emperor began showing visions of the past to Diocletian much as he had done with Ra, indicating that he had become Custodes Tribune following Ra's disappearance into the Webway.{{Fn|1}} 

Now the sole remaining Tribune, Diocletian commanded Custodes forces of the [[Inner Palace]] during the [[Siege of Terra]] and oversaw the defence of the [[Eternity Gate (Imperial)|Eternity Gate]] alongside [[Sanguinius]]. As [[Daemon]]s began manifesting inside the Sanctum itself, Coros went off to seek a "good death", wishing [[Malcador the Sigillite|Malcador]] the same.{{Fn|4}} Diocletian accompanied the Emperor during the teleportation assault aboard the ''[[Vengeful Spirit]]'', becoming scattered from his liege-lord and fighting alongside [[Constantin Valdor]].{{Fn|5}} Finding total madness aboard the ''Vengeful Spirit'', the Custodians were forced to fight in pitch-black against waves of [[Daemon]]s. During the fighting, Coros was brought down despite Valdor's attempts to save him.{{Fn|6}}

Coros and a few other surviving Custodes later make it to [[Lupercal's Court]], where they discover Valdor, Dorn, [[Garviel Loken]], and [[Leetu]] with the bodies of Horus and the Emperor. Seeing the state of the Emperor caused Coros along with Valdor and the other surviving Custodes to weep. Coros was then able to initiate the teleportation that brings the loyalists back to the Imperial Palace.{{Fn|7}}

After the siege, Diocletian met with the now [[Lord Commander of the Imperium]] [[Roboute Guilliman]] frequently to organize the state of the post-war Imperium. Despite these meetings, Diocletian never stopped distrusting and hating the Primarchs for what they had done to the Emperor and His dream and contemplated killing Guilliman out of rage. Afterwards, Diocletian clad himself in the gold of his order once again to journey into the [[Imperial Dungeon]] to visit the now-enthroned Emperor. He then asked the Emperor if He dreamed.{{Fn|8}}

====Legacy====
Diocletian was noted for being one of the few Custodes capable of dreaming and they were reverently written to script. These scripts were then buried in the deepest vaults of the [[Imperial Palace]]'s '''Inner Palace''', along with the recorded dreams of other Custodes.{{Fn|2a}} Later on in his career, Diocletian wrote a seminal work dubbed '''''The Master of Mankind'''''. The book was still read by the Custodes 10,000 years later.{{Fn|2b}}

{{NecromundaPortal}}
[[Image:Djangar.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Djangar{{Fn|1a}}]]
'''Djangar 'Gunfists'''' was the [[Over-tyrant]] of [[House Goliath]] for over ten world cycles, before he was seemingly killed by his successor{{Fn|1a}} [[Rygar Drune]].{{Fn|1b}}

This occurred while they fought in the [[Fist (Necromunda)|Fist]]'s '''Sky-Pit''' arena and [[Rygar Drune|Drune]] sent Djangar tumbling down one of [[Hive Primus]]'s walls. Though Drune declared victory and became the next [[Over-tyrant]], no one realized that Djangar had miraculously survived his fall. He somehow landed on the roof of a [[Ash-hauler]] leaving Hive Primus, though, Djangar was left a mangled wreck and had no memory of who he was when he later awoke. He would heal from his wounds and in time made a new name for himself in the wastes, as Djangar 'Gunfists' the hired gun. During his travels, however, Djangar found himself unknowingly being drawn back to Hive Primus and he eventually entered the [[Hive]] to offer his services. He now works for gangs and [[Merchant Guild|Guilders]], but a few people have recognized [[House Goliath]]'s old [[Over-tyrant]]. Now there are forces moving to take advantage of Djangar's return, and it seems likely a showdown is coming between the massive gunfighter and the current Over-tyrant [[Varran Gor]].{{Fn|1a}}

'''Dogent Krank''' was an [[Imperial Army]] trooper, who was described as having an old soul{{Fn|1b}}, and he served in [[Calth]]'s [[Numinus 61st]] [[Regiment]] during the [[Great Crusade]] and [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|1a}} 
===History===
His [[Regiment]] was part of the [[Ghaslakh Crusade]] that was preparing to launch from [[Calth]], when the [[Word Bearers]] [[Battle for Calth|attacked]] the world, during the [[Horus Heresy]]. As the invasion raged, Krank soon joined a small group of Imperials who escaped with the [[Perpetual]] [[Ollanius Persson]], into a [[Warp Rift]] he created. This began a journey through time and space, as Persson tried to reach [[Terra]] before the traitorous [[Warmaster]] [[Horus]] could kill the [[Emperor]].{{Fn|1b}}

When Ollanius' group arrived on Terra, they found themselves within the clutches of the [[Emperor's Children]] and their dream-garden known as Paradise. Within the horrific realm Krank was badly wounded in an encounter with [[Chaos Space Marine]]s and had to be carried by [[Graft (Servitor)|Graft]].{{Fn|1c}} Krank accompanied the group into the [[Imperial Dungeon]], eventually reaching the [[Golden Throne]] alongside the other "[[Argonauts]]", but discovering that the Emperor had gone to fight Horus aboard the ''[[Vengeful Spirit]]''.{{Fn|2}}

As the group continued on their quest, they were confronted by [[Erebus]] on the walls of the [[Imperial Palace]]. During the subsequent fight most of the group were slain. Krank was slain when the [[Dark Apostle]] issued a word of [[Enuncia]] which blew his head apart.{{Fn|3}}

Dominic Seroff.wikitext:
{{AstraMilitarumPortal}}
'''Dominic Seroff''' was an [[Imperial Guard]] [[Commissar]], a contemporary and later bitter rival of [[Sebastian Yarrick]].


==History==
Seroff was educated at the same [[Schola Progenium]] as Yarrick, and both were selected for the [[Commissariat]] and apprenticed to the legendary [[Lord Commissar]] [[Simeon Rasp]]. At the time of their deployment to [[Mistral (Planet)|Mistral]], Yarrick reflected that, although he did not doubt Seroff's dedication and ability, his appearance was too boyish, almost dandified, for him to be taken seriously as a Commissar.{{Fn|1a}}

===The Second War for Armageddon===
Seroff never forgave Yarrick, and did his utmost to ensure that Yarrick never advanced through the ranks of the Commissariat, and on more than one occasion used his growing influence to assign Yarrick to hazardous missions that would hopefully get him killed. To Seroff's endless vexation, Yarrick always survived.{{Fn|2a}}

The two men met again on [[Armageddon]], by which time Yarrick was still an "ordinary" Commissar, while Seroff had ascended to the rank of Lord Commissar. Seroff's hatred of Yarrick was so vehement that he unconsciously sided with Overlord [[Herman von Strab]] as [[Waaagh! Ghazghkull]] overran the planet. Seroff was no fool, and therefore recognized that every one of von Strab's decisions led to greater and greater disaster for the defending Imperial forces.  As the Commissariat's ranking officer on the planet, Seroff was the only one with the ostensible authority to remove von Strab from command, yet he refused to do so, ignoring the pleas from not just Yarrick, but also [[Princeps]] [[Kurtiz Mannheim]] of the [[Iron Skulls]] [[Titan Legion]], and [[Canoness]] [[Setheno]] of the [[Adepta Sororitas]]. Mannehim noted with frustration that he had come within a hair's breadth of convincing Seroff, until Yarrick's name came up, and Seroff cut him off. Seroff himself questioned the wisdom of his decision, but quickly convinced himself that the "right" thing to do was to hold Yarrick accountable, through any means necessary, for the death and disgrace of Rasp, even if that meant siding with a megalomaniac incompetent like von Strab. Seroff was last seen witnessing, without objection, von Strab's launching of [[virus bomb]] missiles across Armageddon's surface, in the false belief that the munitions were virulent enough to eradicate the invading [[Ork]]s.{{Fn|2}}

Yarrick emerged from the war as one of the greatest heroes not only of Armageddon, but of the entire Imperium. For his complicity with von Strab, Seroff was in total disgrace, and was reassigned to a backwater planet (along with, ironically, another one of Yarrick's nemeses, Inquisitor [[Ingrid Schenk]]). There they were essentially marooned to nurse their hatred for Yarrick and regret their falls from grace. After over a century of exile, the world was suddenly struck by a mysterious plague which rapidly and horrifically killed its victims and mutated inanimate matter. The plague was eventually revealed to be the work of [[Typhus]] who sought to punish Schenk for her expropriation and experimentation with the Plague of Unbelief otherwise known as [[Zombie Plague]], which the [[Herald of Nurgle]] regarded as his own work. Though they both survived the initial outbreak, they were eventually overcome by the raw mutations and delivered to the ''[[Terminus Est]]''. There they briefly encountered Typhus, who taunted and admonished them before triggering their own personalised afflictions, killing Seroff and dragging the tortured and mutated Schenk off to an unknown fate.{{Fn|3}}

("Father" via [[Gene-Seed]]) |Occupation =[[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] of the [[Blood Angels]] [[2nd Company (Blood Angels)|2nd Company]] |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Imperium of Man]] **[[Blood Angels]] |Notes = }} '''Donatos Aphael'''{{Fn|1b}} is the [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] of the [[Blood Angels]] [[2nd Company (Blood Angels)|2nd Company]] and the current [[Master of the Watch]].{{Fn|1a}} As of 999.[[M41]] he has served the Chapter for a century and a half.{{Fn|5}} ==History== He took part in the battle against the [[Necron]] [[World Engine]], in which the [[2nd Company (Blood Angels)|2nd]] and [[4th Company (Blood Angels)|4th]] [[Space Marine Company|Companies]] of the [[Blood Angels]] were deployed against the [[Xenos]]. After the battle was won, it was at Aphael's suggestion that a permanent shrine be raised on [[Safehold]] as a monument to the [[Astral Knights]] [[Chapter]], which had sacrificed every one of its [[Battle-Brother]]s to destroy the Necron menace.{{Fn|1b}} The [[2nd Company (Blood Angels)|2nd Company]] later battled the [[Ork]] [[Warboss]] [[Gutstompa]] in the [[Battle for Antax]]. Like all [[Blood Angels]], Aphael is vulnerable to the [[Red Thirst]] and temporarily succumbed to it in the battle against Gutstompa.{{Fn|1c}} He was also a major Blood Angels commander during the [[Diamor Campaign]]{{Fn|4}}. He is a vocal supporter of the Blood Angels' [[Angels Vermillion]] [[Successor Chapter]], despite knowing [[Commander Dante]] had [[Angels Vermillion#The Sorrowing|ill feelings]] toward them and refused to fight beside the Vermillion. In the [[Red Council]] meeting prior to the [[Devastation of Baal]] though, Aphael asked Dante to call upon their aid, due to [[Hive Fleet Leviathan]]'s massive threat to [[Baal]]. Dante angrily refused to do so, but would not state why and Aphael risked his wrath by repeatedly questioning the Commander's decision. The [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] could not understand that if the Blood Angels were willing to fight beside the [[Necrons]] in the [[Cryptus Campaign]], why would they not fight beside the Vermillion regardless of what fault Dante had with them? However the Commander refused to explain his decision and brought the Council's meeting to an end shortly afterwards.{{Fn|6}} During the [[Battle of Idolatros]] in the [[Arks of Omen Campaign]], Aphael took temporary command of Blood Angels forces following the wounding of [[Dante]] at the hands of [[Angron]].{{Fn|7}} {{Clear}} ==Images== [[Image:Aphael.jpg|thumb|center|220px|Brother-Captain Aphael{{Fn|3}}]] ==See also== *[[List of Space Marine Captains]] ==Sources== *1: [[Codex: Blood Angels (5th Edition)]] **{{Endn|1a}}: pg. 9 **{{Endn|1b}}: pg. 16 **{{Endn|1c}}: pgs. 20–21 *{{Endn|2}}: [[Shield of Baal: Exterminatus]] (E-book), ''Aphael's Blooded'' *{{Endn|3}}: [[Codex: Blood Angels (7th Edition)]] (E-book), ''Sons of Sanguinius'' *{{Endn|4}}: [[Black Crusade: Traitor's Hate]] — Chapter 2 *{{Endn|5}}: [[Black Crusade: Angel's Blade]], pg. 82 *{{Endn|6}}: [[Dante (Novel)]], Chapter 11 *{{Endn|7}}: [[Arks of Omen: The Lion]], pgs. 34-35 {{DEFAULTSORT:Aphael, Donatos}} [[Category:Characters (Blood Angels)]] [[de:Aphael]] [[fr:Donatos Aphael]]

'''Doombreed, the Skull Lord''' is a mighty [[Daemon Prince]] of [[Khorne]], said by some to be older and more powerful than even the [[Daemon]] [[Primarch|Primarchs]]{{Fn|1}}, and wears a cloak made from the skulls of a thousand [[Space Marines]].{{Fn|3}}

===History===
'''Doombreed''' was one of the first of Khorne's servants. His [[True Name]] was long forgotten, remembered only on a scroll of dried skin, but he was once human, a mighty warlord who led armies which ravaged entire nations on [[Terra]] long ago in the [[Age of Terra]] around [[M1]]/[[M2]]{{fn|7b}}. He was responsible for genocide and murder on a grand scale, such wanton carnage drawing the eye of the god [[Khorne]], still relatively young, who granted the warlord the ultimate reward of Daemonhood.{{Fn|1}}{{Fn|4}}

====Horus Heresy====
When [[Accazzar-Beta]] refused to pay fealty to [[Horus]], he led an attack on the world that served as a sacrifice to summon Doombreed. Manifesting from a red pearl, Doombreed slaughtered the entire world while the Warmaster's forces withdrew. [[Argonis]], a [[Herald]] brought to the surface by Horus to witness the summoning of Doombreed, ensured Accazzar-Beta would live forever as an example of the 'Dark Compliance' that awaited any who resisted the Warmaster.{{fn|9}}

Doombreed was present on the ''[[Vengeful Spirit]]'' during the [[Battle of Terra]], witnessing the death of [[Sanguinius]]{{fn|7b}} and fighting against the [[Emperor]] alongside [[N'Kari]].{{Fn|4}}

The [[Sorcerer]] [[Ctesias]] of the [[Thousand Sons]] discovered the True Name of Doombreed, stealing it from a scroll of dried skin. Although he vowed never to release it after realising what it was, he set it free on [[Sortiarius]] when [[Ahzek Ahriman]] returned for the first time since his exile in a bid to undo the [[Rubric of Ahriman|Rubric]]. In the [[Battle of Sortiarius]], Doombreed claimed the 'skull' of the [[Daemon]]-[[Warlord Titan]] ''[[Czetherrtihor]]'' in single combat, raising it in offering to Khorne.{{fn|5}}

====Fifth Black Crusade====
Millennia later, he was summoned by [[Ezekyle Abaddon|Abaddon the Despoiler]] during the [[5th Black Crusade]] by the sacrifice of ten million souls on Tarinth. Promised the skulls of a thousand Space Marines,{{fn|3}} he declared war on the [[Adeptus Astartes]]. During this Crusade two loyal [[Chapter|Chapters]] — the [[Warhawks]] and the [[Venerators]] — were wiped out.{{Fn|2}} A force of [[Blood Angels]] aboard the [[battle barge]] ''[[Eclipse of Hope]]'' went missing{{fn|6}} in the counter-attack against Doombreed, sacrificing their freedom and souls to tether the daemon prince to the planet [[Pallevon]].{{fn|7c}}

====41st Millennium====
Five millennia after its disappearance, the ''Eclipse of Hope'' was encountered by [[Chief Librarian]] [[Mephiston]] of the Blood Angels, leading him to Pallevon.{{fn|6}} There, the Blood Angels encountered a perfect statue of Sanguinius in the moment of his death at Horus' hand - a perfect memory captured in gold, silver, and ruby.{{fn|7a}} Mephiston alone believed the statue to be tainted and attempted to destroy it, but in so doing merely released the daemon prince from his five millennia of imprisonment.{{fn|7b}} Doombreed fought Mephiston, attempting to convince him to join Khorne. The Lord of Death succeeded in banishing the daemon prince, but had set him free.{{fn|7c}}

At the close of the [[M41|41st Millennium]], Doombreed stands at the Warmaster's side once more in the [[Thirteenth Black Crusade]].{{fn|3}} He later appeared at the forefront of Khorne's [[Blood Crusade]].{{Fn|8}}

===Appearance===
Doombreed takes the form of a giant [[Bloodthirster]], wreathed in black smoke which becomes red muscle as he grows ever larger feeding on slaughter. Hooved and winged, his teeth are the size of swords and scraps of flayed fur and skin hang from his wet muzzle.{{fn|5}} He wears brazen Chaos armour resistant to psychic attack, a [[Collar of Khorne]], and a cloak woven with the skulls of a thousand Space Marines{{fn|3}} Alongside a mighty [[Axe of Khorne]] he carries the [[Rod of Khorne]], a massive staff of twisted bone bearing the icon of the Blood God.{{Fn|4}}

(Former) *[[Daemon Prince]] |Gender =Male |Relatives = |Occupation = |Preceded by = |Succeeded by = |Faction ='' '' *[[Chaos]] **[[Slaanesh]] |Notes = }} '''Doomrider''' is a [[Daemon Prince]] of [[Slaanesh]].{{Fn|3}} ===History=== Doomrider's origins are largely a mystery. It is known that he was once a [[Chaos Space Marine]], but anything beyond that is uncertain. According to some, he was once a member of the [[Emperor's Children]] [[Legion]], and lead their debauches during the [[Battle of Terra]]. According to other sources, he was a traitor from a different [[Chapter]], who went renegade after the [[Great Scouring]]. He has many names and titles used by those cultists that pay homage to him including the ''Demon of Speed'', the ''Wolf of the Exhaust'' and the ''King of the Road''.{{Fn|3}} His physical presence when manifested in the material universe is of an angelically beautiful [[Astartes]] warrior clad in baroque [[Power Armour]], his body consumed from within by warpfire. Crowned with horns of onyx, his eyes are burning pits and his mouth is full of jagged fangs. The skin of his face shifts as it constantly regenerates over the damage the warpfire inflicts on his body, creating around him a miasma of exhaust fumes and the stink of burning flesh.{{Fn|3}} Mounted on a Daemonically possessed [[bike]] adorned with deadly blades and spikes and described as part insect, part corpse and part bat - its flaming wheels leave trails of screaming warpfire in its wake.{{Fn|3}} Armed also with his cruel [[Daemon sword]], Doomrider carves a bloody swathe across the battlefield as he mercilessly hunts his prey. He can be summoned by [[Chaos Cultist]]s in foul rituals to aid the forces of Chaos in battle, however he is highly unpredictable in nature and seldom stays in the material universe for very long, often returning to the warp as suddenly as he appears.{{Fn|1}} He has become a target of the [[White Scars]] [[Chapter]], who have sent numerous [[Master of the Hunt]]s after him. All failed, however, to bring his head back to [[Chogoris]], instead returning empty-handed or having their own heads taken and mounted on his Daemonic bike.{{Fn|3}} The latest Huntsman, Captain [[Kor'sarro Khan]], vowed to finally take the Daemon's head. After evading Kor'sarro four previous times, Doomrider was tracked to the [[Imperium]] world of [[Shaka VI]], which had been nearly overwhelmed by a [[Chaos Cult]] empowered by Doomrider. This did not matter to Kor'sarro, who led his brethren against the Cult to reach the Daemon. Though Doomrider would defeat Kor'sarro in the battle, the hunt finally ended when he attempted to drag Kor'sarro through a portal back into the [[Warp]] with him. In a rage Kor'sarro wrapped his hands around Doomrider's neck and ripped the Daemon Prince's head off, closing the portal before they reached it. To Kor'sarro's surprise, Doomrider still lived and his head began to squirm in his hands. Doomrider tried to speak, but the Master of the Hunt quickly crushed his jaw and then returned to his fellow White Scars on the battlefield. With the hunt at an end they returned to Chogoris, taking the still-living head of Doomrider with them.{{Fn|3}} [[Trazyn|Trazyn the Infinite]] is known to keep an exhibit labelled "Doomrider's Folly" in his [[Trazyn#Collection|prismatic galleries]], on the [[Tomb World]] of [[Solemnace]].{{Fn|4}} ===Summoning ritual=== The [[Ordo Malleus]] has been able to translate part of the ritual used to summon Doomrider from the [[Immaterium]].{{Fn|2}} {{QuoteBox |quote = ''''' ''Oh great Lord Slaanesh, send forth your servant, the Daemon Prince Doomrider!'' ''Let our enemies tremble in ruptured awe before his fearsome visage!'' ''Grant them an exquisite death, crushed beneath the flaming wheels of his chromium steed!'' ''Permit them the ecstasy of being slaughtered by Doomrider's throbbing Daemonsword and his pulsating gun of gushing plasma!'' ''Bestow on them one fleeting moment of pleasure as they stare in wonder and orgasmic delight at one of your most divine creations before dying at his hand!'' ''Oh great Lord Slaanesh, for these reasons and many others that tease and titillate our imaginations, we beseech you, send forth your servant, the Daemon Prince Doomrider!''
''Summoning Ritual''{{Fn|2}} |}}{{clear}} ===See Also=== *[[List of Daemon Princes]] ===Sources=== *{{Endn|1}}: [[Codex: Chaos Space Marines (3rd Edition, 1st Codex)]], pg. 24 *{{Endn|2}}: [[White Dwarf 235 (UK)]], pg. 56 *{{Endn|3}}: [[Master of the Hunt (Audio Drama)]] *{{Endn|4}}: [[Codex: Necrons (9th Edition)]], pg. 33 *{{Endn|5}}: [[White Dwarf 235 (UK)]], May 1999, pg. 53 {{ECForces}} [[Category:Characters (Daemon)]] [[Category:Characters (Slaanesh)]] [[fr:Doomrider]]

{{AstraMilitarumPortal}}
[[Imperial Guard Sergeant|Sergeant]] '''Doranz'''{{Fn|Note 1}} was gun commander of a [[Basilisk]] of the [[Ketzok 17th Armoured Regiment]].

==History==
On [[Voltemand]], the 'Serpents' were commanded to travel through the Voltemand Mirewoods to Pavis Crossroads in the Bokore Valley. Once there they were to shell Voltis City and provide artillery cover for infantry operating in the valley.

En route to the Pavis Crossroads, the 'Serpents' were attacked by seven [[World Eater]] Traitor Marines. After losing two [[Basilisk]]s and two guncrews, the [[Tanith First and Only]] emerged from the woods and and killed the Traitor Marines, preventing them from slaughtering the tightly grouped artillery crews.

Doranz was the man to first supply [[Colonel]] [[Colm Corbec]] with his trademark licorice cigars, which he gave as thanks for the counter-ambush.  Doranz's Basilisk transported Corbec and [[Brin Milo]] of the Tanith regiment to their staging point for the assault on Voltis City.  He admitted to being frightened by Milo's [[Tanith Pipes]] during the assault, and he and Corbec bonded over a cigar during the trip.{{Fn|1a}}

Doranz would later take part in the assault on [[Oskray Hive]] on [[Sapiencia]].{{Fn|1b}}

Dorian (Dreadnought).wikitext:
{{UltramarinesPortal}}
'''Honored-ancient Dorian''' was an [[Ultramarines]] [[Contemptor Dreadnought]] in the [[22nd Chapter (Ultramarines Legion)|22nd Chapter]], who took part in the [[Great Crusade]] and [[Calth]]'s [[Underground War]], during the [[Horus Heresy]].{{Fn|1}}


==Biography==
After the [[Word Bearers]] had corrupted [[Calth]]'s sun, [[Veridia]], into giving off deadly radiation, the [[Ultramarines]] trapped on on the world sought refuge beneath its surface. [[Consul-Chaplain]] [[Ankarion]] successfully led the remnants of the [[Space Marine Legion|Legion]]'s [[Space Marine Company|547th Company]] to the '''Auroran arcology''', which also sheltered two hundred thousand of Calth's population. The Company then sent a request for immediate aid, but due to the incursions by the World Bearers, who also sought to escape Veridian's radiation, the Ultramarines' central command on Calth lost contact with Auroran. As their request bore the Legion's highest priority, Thesian was sent to investigate what had happened to the archeology. Commanding the [[22nd Chapter (Ultramarines Legion)|22nd Chapter]]'s [[Destroyer Marine|4th Destroyer]] [[Space Marine Company|Company]], he entered Ankarion and his forces were quickly attacked by the Word Bearers and the 547th's [[Possession|animated]] corpses. Dorian and his fellow [[Dreadnought]] [[Andronicus (Dreadnought)|Andronicus]] had been attached to the 4th Destroyer Company during this battle and their firepower greatly aided in killing numerous foes. Thanks to the two's efforts, the Company succeeded in fighting their way to the former headquarters of the 547th, which had been turned into a fane to the [[Chaos God]] [[Nurgle]]. They also found Ankarion there, standing besides a group of Word Bearers and [[Chaos]] icons. But the Consul-Chaplain now wore a suit of crimson [[power armor]] and his helmet was an indistinguishable mass of eyes, fanged mouths and curving horns. As Dorian and the 4th Destroyer Company realized Ankarion had betrayed the [[Ultramarines]], the corrupted [[Chaplain]] bellowed a challenge in ancient [[Colchis|Colchisian]] and charged at them. The Word Bearers and the animated corpses of the 547th followed him, along with [[Daemon]]s made from shadows.{{Fn|1}} 

However the [[Destroyer Marine|4th Destroyer]] [[Space Marine Company|Company]] charged at Ankarion's forces as well, as they had become enraged that a fellow [[Ultramarine]] was responsible for the '''Auroran arcology''''s corruption. [[Space Marine Captain|Captain]] [[Valius Thesian]] and Ankarion then dueled each other, but the fallen [[Chaplain]] fatally wounded Thesian with an obsidian spear. With the last of his strength, though, the Captain activated a [[melta bomb]], which consumed both him and Ankarion. The fighting between their surviving forces continued, but [[Andronicus (Dreadnought)|Andronicus]] began a wild rampage after Dorian was killed during the battle. The enraged [[Contemptor Dreadnought]] tore apart multiple foes and also destroyed a [[Chaos]] icon within the fane. Its destruction, though, put an end to the 547th's [[Possession|animated]] corpses and allowed the 4th Destroyer Company to defeat the remaining Word Bearers.{{Fn|1}}

Doyl.wikitext:
{{TanithPortal}}
'''Doyl''' was a [[Imperial Guard Scout|Scout]]{{Fn|1}} of the [[Tanith First and Only]] [[Imperial Guard Regiment|regiment]].{{Fn|1}}{{Fn|2a}}


==Biography==
When the ''First and Only'' were deployed in the [[Phantine (Planet)|Phantine]] theatre, Doyl was one of sixteen Tanith selected personally by [[Colonel-Commissar]] [[Ibram Gaunt]] to take part in [[Operation Larisel]].{{Fn|2b}} Alongside [[Trooper]]s [[Brin Milo|Milo]] and [[Nessa]] and the [[Phantine Skyborne|Skyborne Specialist]] [[Lex Cardinale|Cardinale]], Doyl was assigned to team ''Larisel 3'' under [[Sergeant (Imperial Guard)|Sergeant]] [[Adare]].{{Fn|2c}}{{Fn|2d}}

After successfully infiltrating the [[Blood Pact]]-held city of [[Ouranberg]]{{Fn|2d}}, Larisel 3 tried to make their way through the city by blending in with a work party of enslaved [[Imperial citizen]]s.{{Fn|2e}} However, Milo and Nessa were separated from the group and, while looking for them, Cardinale was struck by a Blood Pact slaver with an [[electro-lash]]. This made him drop his [[aquila]] pendant and, when the slavers discovered it, they raised the alarm and unleashed [[cyber-mastiff]]s to track him down. Doyl and Adare were forced to break cover to save Cardinale from being mauled to death by the hate-dogs and this led to a firefight while they tried to get to safety. Ultimately, Doyl and Adare were cut down by [[loxatl]] mercenaries.{{Fn|2e}}

Drach'nyen.wikitext:
{{BlackLegionPortal}}
[[Image:Daemon Sword Drach'nyen.png|thumb|500px|The Daemon Sword Drach'nyen{{fn|5}}]]
'''Drach'nyen''', '''the End of Empires''' and the '''Echo of the First Murder''', is an ancient [[daemon]] of pure, unadulterated malice currently bound in the [[daemon sword]] of the same name wielded by [[Abaddon the Despoiler]].{{Fn|2}}

==Appearance==
[[Image:DrachArt.jpg|thumb|200px|Drach'nyen]]
'''Drach'nyen''' can take many forms, and it only appears as a great blade in the hands of Abaddon because that is how the Warmaster chooses it to be. In truth, the sword has no real shape or size, at least nothing that could be understood by the mind of man.{{Fn|3}}

The weapon normally appears to be something akin to a two-handed sword, except that Abaddon wields the weapon with a single hand in conjunction with the [[Talon of Horus]].  The guard of the weapon tends to be golden in colour, with a leering face of a demon just above the handle. The ricasso of the weapon has spikes protruding from the sides as well as outward from the blade, and the blade itself is blue with red, tormented faces (the faces of souls it has devoured since being claimed by Abaddon{{Fn|5}}) writhing across its surface.{{Fn|1}}

== History ==
The origins of Drach'nyen are a mystery to most, unknown perhaps even to Abaddon himself. Daemons speak of the blade in fear, calling it the ''Thorn in Reality'' or the ''Shard of Madness''. It is, however, known to be a weapon that has existed long before the rise of [[Human|Mankind]].{{Fn|3}}

===The First Murder===
Drach'nyen was born at the moment of the first murder - the first time a human killed another human outside of the need to survive. The name Drach'nyen, which can be translated as ''the End of Empires''{{Fn|4b}}, is an approximation of the scream of the first murderer and that of the brother he murdered.{{Fn|4a}}

===War Within the Webway===
{{Spoiler|source=Master of Mankind (Novel)}}
During the [[Horus Heresy]], Drach'nyen entered the human portion of the [[webway]]. The [[Emperor of Mankind]] was able to sense its presence, and knew it was the daemon born of the first murder.{{Fn|4b}} Shortly after its arrival, the daemonic forces were able to overwhelm the Imperial forces at [[Calastar]], forcing them to retreat to the [[Imperial Palace]]. In order to cover the retreat, the Emperor left the [[Golden Throne]] to confront Drach'nyen. The daemon took the form of a Stone Epoch war-chief, impaling the Emperor and claiming it would be His death. The Emperor ripped the daemon, now in the form of the daemon sword, from His body and hurled it at the [[Adeptus Custodes|Custodian]] [[Ra Endymion]], impaling him and binding it within him. As the last Imperial forces retreated from the webway, He order Ra to run.{{fn|4c}}

Later during the [[Siege of Terra]], the host of Drach'nyen manifested upon the Throneworld to lead an army of Daemons.{{Fn|7}}

===Abaddon's Claim===
[[Image:Mtg-drach-nyen.jpg|right|thumb|Abaddon retrieving Drach'nyen{{fn|8}}]]
At some point, Drach'nyen was bound in the labyrinth beneath the [[Tower of Silence]] on [[Uralan]], where the [[Chaos Gods]] themselves lock away their secrets. Abaddon was led to the Tower of Silence during his [[1st Black Crusade]] in 781.[[M31]] and, after fighting off constructs of dark energy that served as the tower's guardians, entered the mirrored heart of Uralan beneath the crypts. Wandering a haunted labyrinth of impossible angles that was continuously made and unmade as he walked, Abaddon encountered a towering figure wreathed in golden light. The golden figure led him to the centre of the labyrinth, where a shard of shifting darkness hung. When Abaddon grasped it, Drach'nyen took on the form of a fearsome blade.{{Fn|3}}

After that, Drach'nyen served Abaddon well. With it Abaddon hewed open the gates of the [[Kromarch]]'s citadel, disrupting the nullification fields with which they were reinforcing the fabric of realspace. Another famous story tells about the impaling of the [[Great Technomandrite]] of [[Danth]], thus sealing the fate of the anti-empyric [[Lemuel Cluster]].{{Fn|6}}
